$description: Tanrei tokens resolved for scheme "light-high". Generated; do not edit.

gap.$description: Between the icon, the text, the trailing text and the chevron of a header: a navigation drawer row's gap.

shape.$description: The corners of a header's container, which its state layer and its focus indicator follow. Square in the default system, as a list item's row is: a header reaches both edges of its item, and in the outlined look the edge's corners clip it.

color.$description: The line between two items where separation is divider: the one hairline.

gap.$description: Between two items where separation is gap.

disclosure-duration.$description: How long an item takes to open or close: its content revealed or hidden, what follows moving, and its chevron turning. The name and the value of a navigation drawer group's.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

state-duration.$description: How long a state change of a header takes.

color.$description: The edge of the outlined look: the one hairline, the color a divider, an outlined card and an outlined callout draw theirs in. Decorative: the headers are told as buttons by their chevrons and their states. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

shape.$description: The corners of the outlined look's edge: the step of a card and of a callout, so that a bounded block of content reads as one of the page's blocks.

color.$description: The chevron: a mark, quieter than the label, in the color a navigation drawer draws a group's chevron in.
No fill inside the edge either, in the default system. It is a token of its own so that a system can tint the header of a bounded item.
The label: the text color of the surface the accordion stands on.
What hover, focus and press mix into the header: the label's color.
The chevron: a mark, quieter than the label, in the color a navigation drawer draws a group's chevron in.
The label: the text color of the surface the accordion stands on.
What hover, focus and press mix into the header: the label's color.

separation.$description: How an item is told from the item next to it. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color between them. gap: item.gap of empty space and no line; in the outlined look each item then has an edge of its own. Follows the system's choice; an accordion's separation prop overrides it (ACC-10). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between two actions.
Between the navigation slot, the title block and the actions slot.

padding-block-end.$description: Below the expanded title of a large bar.

padding-inline.$description: From the start and end edges to the navigation and actions slots.

condition-duration.$description: How long the bar takes to change between flat and scrolled.

width.$description: The bar's bottom edge.

inset.$description: The title's start inset when the navigation slot is empty, and the expanded title's start inset in a large bar.

gap.$description: Distance between the main content and an aside stacked above or below it. A dividing line, where one is drawn, runs in its middle.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of the aside's content from the start and the end of its column while it stands beside the main content.

width.$description: The width of the aside beside the main content, its insets included, where what it holds has no width of its own. The navigation drawer's width in the default system, so that the frame is even on both sides.

expanded.$description: The window width from which the class is expanded: the navigation and the aside stand beside the main content.

medium.$description: The window width from which the class is medium. Below it the window is compact: one column, the navigation over the content, a navigation bar at the bottom where the product gives one.

color.$description: The frame's fill: what shows wherever no region draws a fill of its own, and under the system insets.
The text color the frame hands to what it holds, as the inherited foreground. Prose and plain content bring none of their own.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the footer's content.

max-width.$description: The greatest width of the main region's content while mainWidth is contained: the prose's measure at the default text size with room for the blocks that are wider than text (a table, a code block, a figure).

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the main region's content, and above and below the content of an aside that stands beside it, so that their first lines are level.

color.$description: The color of the lines the shell draws between regions: the system's one hairline.

width.$description: The thickness of those lines, and of the edge the skip link's box gains in a forced-colors mode.

separation.$description: How regions that touch are told apart. divider: a line of outline.width in outline.color above the footer, at the start edge of an aside beside the main content, and between the main content and a stacked aside. gap: no line, the same spaces. Follows the system's choice; the shell's separation prop overrides it (APS-18). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The fill of the box the focused skip link is shown in: a raised surface, on which a standard Link is readable.

elevation.$description: How far the box is raised: above a sticky header and everything else in the frame.

padding-block.$description: Inset of the link from the top and the bottom of the box: with one line of the label's text style the box reaches the pointer target's height.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of the link from the start and the end of the box.

shape.$description: The box's corners: the corner of a control.

typescale.$description: The text style of the skip link in its box. Its color, underline and focus ring are the Link's own.

offset.$description: Distance of the box from the top and the start edges of the window, inside the system insets.

color.$description: The fill behind the initials, behind the glyph, behind a picture that is still loading and behind the transparent parts of a picture: the quiet tone a list row puts behind its leading avatar. The same for every person.
The color of that gap: the surface the group sits on, as a badge's outline is. A product that places a group on another surface sets that surface's color here for that place.

width.$description: The width of the gap a group draws around each of its avatars, outside the avatar's edge, so two pictures that overlap are read as two.

color.$description: The color of the fallback glyph: the initials' color.
The color of the initials and of a group's count: secondary content on the quiet fill.

height.$description: The count pill's minimum height; also its minimum width, so a single digit sits in a circle.

offset.$description: How far the center of the pill's leading circle (a container.height square at its start) sits inside the anchor's top-end corner, on both axes. A longer count grows toward the end, away from the anchor.
How far the dot's center sits inside the anchor's top-end corner, on both axes.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot shown when there is no count.

width.$description: Drawn outside the container (dot or pill), so it does not change the badge's size or where it sits.

elevation.$description: The sheet's lift over the content it covers. Tanrei's level1 is only the hairline ring, so a sheet that must stand apart from a page with no scrim under it rests at level2; a system whose level1 is a real shadow may set level1.

margin-block-start.$description: At full height, the distance kept between the sheet's top edge and the top of the area it covers (below the top system inset), so that the page behind is still seen to be there.

max-width.$description: The widest a sheet draws; on a wider area it is centred and the area shows at its sides.

padding.$description: While inset is true: the inset of the content from the sheet's start, end and bottom edges, and from its top edge when there is no drag handle.

partial-fraction.$description: At partial height, the fraction of the area's height the sheet takes (when its content is taller than that).

shape.$description: The corners at the sheet's top edge; its bottom corners meet the screen's edge and stay square.

color.$description: The foreground the sheet hands to its content, as the platform's inherited color.
The handle's box at rest: nothing is drawn; its states draw the state layer.
The grip is how a sighted person finds a control, so it takes the functional boundary role (3:1 on every surface), not the decorative hairline.

container-height.$description: The height of the drag handle's box. With the margins above and below it, the handle's row is the touch target's height.

container-width.$description: The drag handle's box: where its hover, focus and press are drawn, centred on the grip.

grip-width.$description: The drawn grip: the short bar that says the sheet can be dragged.

margin-block.$description: Above and below the drag handle's box: from the sheet's top edge, and to the content.

enter-duration.$description: How long the sheet takes to rise into place (and a modal sheet's scrim to fade in), to move to another height, or to settle after a drag: the modal layer's, so that every modal surface of a product keeps one tempo.

exit-duration.$description: How long the sheet takes to leave below the bottom edge (and a modal sheet's scrim to fade out): the modal layer's.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press on the drag handle takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

blur.$description: How much the scrim behind a modal sheet blurs what lies behind it: the modal layer's (0, none, in the default system).

color.$description: The dim over everything behind a modal sheet, alpha included: the modal layer's, unless a system sets the bottom sheet apart. A standard sheet draws none.

gap.$description: Space between a level's glyph and its label.

shape.$description: The corners of the shape that carries hover, focus and press behind a level that is a link and behind the overflow button, and of the focus ring around it.

color.$description: The current page: the color of the text around it, because it is where the person is and not somewhere to go.
Used only where the product gives the current page a destination, so that it is a link.

size.$description: The box of a level's glyph and of the overflow button's glyph.

color.$description: The fill behind a level that is a link. None at rest: it is where hover, focus and press are drawn.
The label, the underline and the glyph of a level that is a link: the role the vocabulary keeps for text links.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container.
A level above the current page that has no destination: secondary text, not a link.

typescale.$description: The text style of every level.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple: the pressed layer grows from the point of contact over this time, with state-easing. Unused by the other choices.

color.$description: The glyph of the button that stands for the collapsed levels: a glyph alone is a step quieter than a word.

row-gap.$description: Space between two lines of a trail that wraps.

color.$description: The separator between two levels. Decorative.

gap.$description: Space between a separator and the level on either side of it.

size.$description: The separator glyph's box.

offset.$description: How far below the text's baseline the underline is drawn.

visibility.$description: When the underline of a level that is a link is drawn. always: at rest and in every state. hover: while the level is hovered, focused from the keyboard or pressed, and not at rest. never: in no state. Follows the system's choice; a trail's underline prop overrides it (BRC-30). Forced colors draw it under every choice (BRC-24). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

width.$description: The thickness of the underline of a level that is a link. The underline takes the label's color in every state.

color.$description: The line on a seam under divider, between two items that rest on the same fill and are not both emphasis fills (BGR-24): outlined, text, tonal and elevated Buttons, and unselected toggles. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in and the color of an outlined Button's outline, so an outlined group reads as one outline with rules in it. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw the rules apart from its dividers.

inset.$description: How far the line stops short of each end of the seam: from the top and the bottom of a row, from the start and the end of a column. 0 draws it across the whole seam. Above 0 the group reads as one shape with rules in it rather than as shapes cut apart, which is what tells divider from a narrow gap.

color.$description: The line on a seam between two items that both rest on an emphasis fill: two filled Buttons, or two selected toggles (BGR-24). The hairline is a faint darkening of a light ground or a faint lightening of a dark one and cannot be seen on these fills (1.0–1.1:1), so the line there takes the functional outline role, which is told from them.

thickness.$description: The thickness of the line on a seam.

gap.$description: Space between two joined items, in a row or a column, under gap. Unused under divider, where the items touch.

outer-inset.$description: Padding added to the first item at its start and to the last item at its end in a joined row (BGR-23). A full outer end takes more of the container away beside the content than the tighter inner corner does, so equal paddings look unequal; this evens them. A system whose outer ends are no rounder than its inner corners sets 0.

outer-shape.$description: The radius of the outer ends of a joined row: the start corners of the first item and the end corners of the last, capped at half the item's height (BGR-2). Full, so the row reads as one pill with seams.

inner-shape.$description: The radius of the corners where two joined items face each other, in a row or a column, under gap. Under divider those corners are square.

separation.$description: How the items of a connected group are joined. divider: they touch, with a line on each seam and square inner corners. gap: they stand connected.gap apart, with connected.inner-shape where they face each other and nothing drawn between them. Follows the system's choice; a group's separation prop overrides it (BGR-21). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

outer-shape.$description: The radius of the outer ends of a joined column: the top corners of the first item and the bottom corners of the last (BGR-16). Two steps above the inner corner and short of full, so the column reads as one rounded panel with seams rather than a capsule.

gap.$description: Space between the visible bounds of two items of a standard group, side by side or one above the other. Neighbouring hit areas meet at the middle of it (BGR-4), so it is what keeps each item's target whole: at sys.target.touch minus an item's width (in a row) or height (in a column) or more, the item keeps its full target between neighbours. The default system's 16 is 48 minus its narrowest and lowest item (a small icon-only Button, 32).

inner-gap.$description: The space between the two halves under gap. Neither half's outline nor elevation ring reaches into it. Unused under divider, where the halves touch.

inner-shape.$description: The corners where the two halves face each other, under gap: a small step, so the seam reads against the round ends. Under divider those corners are square.

inner-shape-open.$description: The trailing half's inner corners while the menu is open, under gap. The same as inner-shape by default: the trailing half keeps its shape, and the chevron alone shows that the menu is open. A system whose trailing half rounds into a shape of its own while open sets container.shape here.

outer-inset.$description: Padding added to the leading half at its start and to the trailing half at its end, at either trailing width (SPB-32). A full outer end takes more of the container away beside the content than the tighter inner corner does, so equal paddings look unequal; this evens them, as the connected button group does. A system whose outer ends are no rounder than its inner corners sets 0.

separation.$description: How the two halves are joined. divider: they touch, with a line on the seam and square inner corners. gap: they stand inner-gap apart, with inner-shape where they face each other and nothing drawn between them. Follows the system's choice; an instance's separation prop overrides it (SPB-30). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

shape.$description: The outer corners: the leading half's start corners and the trailing half's end corners. Capped at half a half's height, so full draws round ends.

inset.$description: How far the line stops short of the top and of the bottom of the seam. 0 draws it across the whole seam. The same as the connected button group's by default, so the two joined controls are ruled alike.

thickness.$description: The thickness of the line on the seam under divider.

elevation.$description: Under gap its ring is drawn inside each half's edge and only the blurred layers fall outside; under divider no ring is drawn along the seam (SPB-18, SPB-26).

color.$description: The line on the seam under divider. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in: it reads on this container as it does on a surface.
The label, the icon and the chevron.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a half's container: its label color.

The line on the seam under divider. It is the functional outline role and not the hairline the other variants use: the hairline is a faint darkening of a light ground or a faint lightening of a dark one, and cannot be seen on this container (1.0:1 in every scheme of the default system).
The label, the icon and the chevron.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a half's container: its label color.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the ripple takes to spread.

hover-close-delay.$description: How long a menu opened on hover stays open after the pointer has left both the trailing half and the menu, so the pointer can cross onto the menu or slip off an edge and come back (WCAG 1.4.13, hoverable).

hover-open-delay.$description: Where hoverOpen is on and hoverDelay is not set: how long a fine pointer rests on the trailing half before the menu opens, so that a pointer passing over it does not open one.

open-duration.$description: The chevron turning or cross-fading to its open form, and the trailing half's inner corners changing where inner-shape-open differs from inner-shape, when the menu opens or closes.

color.$description: The line on the seam under divider: the outline's own color, so the control reads as one outline with a rule in it.
The label, the icon and the chevron.

The edge of the outlined variant. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in, as the outlined Button's is. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw the edge apart from its dividers.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a half's container: its label color.
The line on the seam under divider. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in: it reads on this container as it does on a surface.
The label, the icon and the chevron.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a half's container: its label color.

thickness.$description: The arc's stroke: the small loading indicator's.

shape.$description: The corners. Fully rounded in the default system: a button with a label is a pill, an icon-only button, which is as wide as it is high, a circle. A smaller corner draws a rounded rectangle and a rounded square.

color.$description: The glyph of an icon-only button; beside a label the icon takes label.color. The label's color by default.
A raised toggle that is on takes the primary fill, as a filled one does; it keeps its elevation.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container. Button's state layer is its label color.
The glyph of an icon-only button; beside a label the icon takes label.color. The label's color by default.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container. Button's state layer is its label color.
A toggle that is off is quieter than a filled action: a neutral fill, not the primary one.

busy-cycle-duration.$description: One turn of the busy arc (BTN-36): the loading indicator's. Under reduced motion it does not turn, and its opacity eases once per this time instead.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple: the pressed layer grows from the point of contact over this time, with state-easing. Unused by the other choices.

color.$description: The glyph of an icon-only button; beside a label the icon takes label.color. A glyph alone in an unfilled button is a step quieter than a label, as the icon actions of a toolbar or a row are.

The edge of an outlined button. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in: one quiet line across the product. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw the edge apart from its dividers.
An outlined toggle that is on fills with the inverse surface and drops its border.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container. Button's state layer is its label color.
The glyph of an icon-only button; beside a label the icon takes label.color. A glyph alone with no container is a step quieter than a label, as the icon actions of a toolbar or a row are.
A text toggle that is on is told from one that is off by a stronger content color and a filled glyph; it grows no container.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container. Button's state layer is its label color.
The glyph of an icon-only button; beside a label the icon takes label.color. The label's color by default.
In the neutral default, secondary-container equals surface-container-highest (the unselected fill), so the selected fill is a different step.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container. Button's state layer is its label color.
Quieter than a day of the month, and still held to text contrast, because it can be chosen.

size.$description: The side of the square each weekday name and each day occupies, and the height of a row of years. Never smaller than the minimum target: the cells are the days' hit areas and cannot extend over each other.

shape.$description: A day is pressed like a button, so a circle in the default system.

size.$description: The side of a day's container, and the height of the band that joins a range, 40.

color.$description: The band that joins the days of a range, drawn across their whole cells. surface-dim recedes from the surface in every scheme, where the tonal containers are within a step or two of surface-bright in the dark default.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

page-duration.$description: How long a month change takes — the weeks' scroll on the vertical axis, the pages' slide on the horizontal one, and the settling or the return after a drag is released — and the day and year views' cross-fade.

axis.$description: The axis months move along. vertical: the previous button points up and the next down, the weeks scroll as one column from one month to the next (a week two months share is one row, the days coming into view fade in and a neighbouring month's day changes into one of the month's own as the weeks move), and a vertical scroll or drag moves the month. horizontal: the buttons point back and forward, a later month's page slides in from the end, and a horizontal scroll or drag moves the month. A drag is followed on either axis. The arrow keys move by day and week, and Page Up and Page Down by month, on either axis. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between the previous and next buttons.

width.$description: The ring a day or year container draws in its condition's outline color (today's ring in the default).

height.$description: The least height of the month-and-year button; its hit area extends to the minimum target.

shape.$description: A button-like control, so a pill in the default system.

gap.$description: Between the month and year and the chevron.

shape.$description: A year is pressed like a button, so a pill in the default system.

gap.$description: Between the text and the row of actions below it.

item-gap.$description: Between two actions, along the row and between rows when they wrap.

color.$description: The glyph on the tonal container, in that container's content color.

tonal.$description: The quiet neutral fill, the one a tonal tag without a status draws.

gap.$description: Between the text and the close button.

padding-block.$description: Above the first line and below the last block. With the body's text style this puts the first line where a snackbar's is.

padding-inline.$description: Before the glyph or, without one, the text, and after the text where there is no close button.

padding-inline-end-with-close.$description: After the close button: tighter than after text, because the button's own shape already holds its glyph away from the edge.

shape.$description: The container's corners: the step of a card and of a snackbar, so a block of content reads as one of the page's blocks and not as a control.

height.$description: The side of the close button's square. Its hit area meets the minimum target.

size.$description: The close glyph: the size of the callout's own glyph.

shape.$description: The corners of the close button's state layer: a circle in the default system, as an icon-only button.

outlined.$description: The surface's text color: a status does not color long text.
No fill, as the outlined look without a status.

tonal.$description: On a status's container the indicator takes that container's content color, which every system holds against it.

outlined.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity: the only place an outlined callout shows its status.

tonal.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity.

outlined.$description: The outlined look sits on a surface, where the system's own focus color is held.

tonal.$description: On the tonal container the indicator takes the container's content color, which every system holds against it.

gap.$description: Between the glyph and the text after it, as in a snackbar.

opacity.$description: The opacity the glyph is drawn at, applied to the glyph color of the form: a mark beside the text, a little softer than the text, by the amount a snackbar softens its own. The glyph so drawn keeps 3:1 against its container in every form and scheme of the default system.

size.$description: The glyph's box: one line of the medium body text, so the glyph sits on the first line without pushing it.

outlined.$description: The surface's text color: a status does not color long text.
No fill, as the outlined look without a status.

tonal.$description: On a status's container the indicator takes that container's content color, which every system holds against it.

outlined.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity: the only place an outlined callout shows its status.

tonal.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press on the close button takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

color.$description: The edge of the outlined look, in every status: the one hairline, the color a divider and an outlined tag draw theirs in. Decorative: the glyph and the words carry the meaning. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

outlined.$description: The surface's text color: a status does not color long text.
No fill, as the outlined look without a status.

tonal.$description: On a status's container the indicator takes that container's content color, which every system holds against it.

outlined.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity: the only place an outlined callout shows its status.

tonal.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity.

gap.$description: Between the title and the body below it.

outlined.$description: The surface's text color: a status does not color long text.

outlined.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity: the only place an outlined callout shows its status.

tonal.$description: The status glyph, in the status's own color, drawn at icon.opacity.

padding.$description: Inset of the content on every side while inset is true. Content that bleeds to the edges (media) sets inset to false and may read this token to pad its own text.

elevation.$description: The elevated card's resting depth. Tanrei's level1 is only the hairline ring, which on a white surface draws exactly the outlined card, so it rests at level2; a system whose level1 is a real shadow (m3-like, cupertino) sets level1.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

interval.$description: How long the row rests at an item before autoplay moves on, unless the product gives the carousel another (autoplayInterval).

large-width.$description: The width the hero is laid out at, and every item's width while widths are fixed, unless the product gives the carousel another (itemWidth). With fluid widths the hero is kept between a floor and a cap (CRL-9).

min-scale.$description: While the other items are drawn smaller (scaleOthers), the scale of an item one position or more from the hero; between the two the scale follows the scroll. The gap to its neighbours stays layout.gap, and its corners keep container.shape (CRL-26).

shape.$description: An item's corners, which clip its content.

small-max-width.$description: With fluid widths, the widest a small slot is made (CRL-10 lets it grow past this only in the cases it names); the hero's cap leaves one small slot this wide on each side where items follow.

small-min-width.$description: With fluid widths, the narrowest a small slot may be: enough to show that more follows and, with the gap, to be pressed. An item is narrower only on its way in or out at an edge (CRL-12).

button-size.$description: The playback control's square, and the height of the dots' container, 40, around a 24 glyph.

height.$description: The controls row below the items, drawn while the dots or the playback control are. As tall as a touch target, so both controls keep their whole target inside it.

size.$description: The pause and play glyphs: an icon-only button's medium glyph.

indicator-padding-inline.$description: Between the dots' ends and the ends of their container, which shows hover, focus and press.

shape.$description: The corners of the playback control and of the dots' container: a circle and a pill, as button-like controls are in the default system.

active-width.$description: The width of the current dot, fully stretched. Its shape, not its color alone, tells it apart (WCAG 1.4.1); a width equal to size draws no stretch.

color.$description: Every dot but the current one, and the unfilled part of the current dot while autoplay progress is shown. The functional outline role: the dots are a control, held to 3:1 against the surface.

gap.$description: Between two dots.

size.$description: A dot's diameter, and the height of every dot, stretched or not.

color.$description: Behind the dots: no fill at rest; hover, focus and press show on it.
The current dot, and the fill of autoplay progress. Other dots are dot.color.
Behind an item's content: what shows while an image loads, around content that does not fill the item, and under the state layer.
The foreground the carousel hands to an item's content, as the platform's inherited color.

gap.$description: Between two neighbouring items, from drawn edge to drawn edge, at every scroll position and at every scale (CRL-40). Half of it on each side completes a small item's touch target (CRL-4).

height.$description: The height of the row of items, and so of the items, unless the product sizes the carousel through the platform's own sizing. The controls row, when drawn, is added below it.

padding-inline.$description: Between each of the carousel's edges and the inner width the slots are laid out in. Items scroll under it to the carousel's edges; it is not a clip, and with fluid widths nothing is drawn in it at rest. The playback control sits inside it.

autoplay-duration.$description: How long an automatic advance takes (and the return to the first item when the row does not loop).

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

scroll-duration.$description: How long the row takes to settle at an item after a drag, or to bring an item into place when it takes focus or the dots move it.

color.$description: The playback control has no fill at rest, as an icon-only text Button.
The pause and play glyphs: an icon-only text Button's glyph color.

gap.$description: The space between two neighbours of one group of actions — the attach button and the leading actions; the counter, the trailing actions and the send button — and between two lines of actions that wrapped. With a medium Button it sets neighbours sys.target.touch apart from centre to centre, so each keeps its whole target.
In the inline layout, the space between the typing area and the group of actions before it, and between the typing area and the group after it.

height.$description: The capsule's least height: the height it has with one line of text, no attachment and the actions on the text's line. The Button's large and the search bar's, so a composer shares a row with them; with container.padding-block it leaves room for a medium Button. Half of it is the capsule's radius at every height (container.shape).

padding-block.$description: From the capsule's top and bottom edges to what it holds: the row of actions, the typing area, the strip.

padding-inline.$description: From the capsule's start or end edge to the typing area where the typing area is the outermost part on that side, and to the strip of attachments: text and pictures stand clear of the rounded corner.

padding-inline-with-button.$description: From the capsule's start or end edge to a Button that is the outermost part on that side. With container.padding-block of the same value a round Button sits concentric in the capsule's end, and has its whole target on that side: half of sys.target.touch minus half of the Button's width, or more.

row-gap.$description: In the stacked layout, the space between the line that holds the typing area and the send button and the row of actions below it, in addition to the typing area's own input.padding-block.

shape.$description: The largest radius of the capsule's corners. The capsule never draws more than half the height it has with one line (CCM-41), so the full step gives a capsule that is fully rounded while it holds one line and keeps exactly those corners as it grows; a smaller step gives a rounded box at every height.

color.$description: The count while the text is within the limit, or there is none: secondary content.
The count while the text is longer than the limit: the error role, used for errors and nothing else. The two numbers say the same without the color.

typescale.$description: The count of characters and the limit: the text style a field's own count is written in.

color.$description: The capsule's fill in error: unchanged. The error is said by the edge.

elevation.$description: The capsule's lift in error: as standard.

color.$description: The capsule's edge in error, at rest and focused: the error role, used for errors and nothing else, so that the capsule itself is marked and not only a text beside it.
As standard.state-layer.color.

padding-block.$description: Above the first line and below the last line of the typing area. With one line of the typing's text style it makes the typing area as tall as a medium Button, so the line and the Buttons beside it share a centre; as lines are added the last line keeps that place.

inline-min-width.$description: The capsule's own inline size under which the inline layout is drawn stacked: every action but the send button moves to a row below the typing area, which shares its line with the send button alone. A width of the composer, not of the window, and not a size of anything drawn. It grows with enlarged text, so a composer whose text has doubled stacks sooner.

state-duration.$description: How long the capsule's edge and fill take to change between rest, hover, focus, error and the receiving condition, and the counter to change color.

width.$description: The capsule's edge at rest; its focused width is a state token.

color.$description: The capsule's fill while it will take what is dragged over it: the quiet selection, because the composer is the place now chosen. The fill the file picker's drop area has in the same condition.
The capsule's edge in that condition: the content color of the quiet selection.

width.$description: The width of that edge: the thick border, so that the condition is told by more than a change of fill.

variant.$description: The Button variant of the send button the composer brings, an icon-only medium Button (CCM-6), and of the stop button in its place (CCM-17). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The capsule's fill: the fill of the search bar and of a text input's box, so that every place a person types into is one surface.

elevation.$description: The capsule's lift: none in Tanrei. A composer that floats over the end of a conversation is raised.

color.$description: The capsule's edge at rest: none. The capsule is marked by its fill; its edge appears as its focus indicator.
The color hover mixes into the capsule: the color of what is typed in it, as the search bar's and a text input's. Focus mixes nothing: the edge answers it.

gap.$description: The space between two File items of the strip, along a line and between two lines of it.

offset.$description: Between the strip and what stands below it in the capsule: the typing area, or the row that holds it.

padding-block-start.$description: Above the strip, in addition to container.padding-block: it keeps the corner of the first tile inside the capsule's rounded corner.

shape.$description: The corner of the box, 2: one unit of the roundness dial, below the corner scale's first step (extra-small, 3), which on an 18 box reads too round for a checkbox.

size.$description: The side of the visible box, 18.
The round state layer behind the box, 40. With the label gap it ends where the 48 touch target does, so the label starts at the target's edge.

gap.$description: From the container to the label.

typescale.$description: The visible label.

size.$description: The glyph box of the check and the dash (the icon set's check and remove), centered on the box. 20 on an 18 box: a glyph's box is larger than its ink, so the icon set's check drawn at 20 keeps its ink inside the box.

weight.$description: The weight the check and the dash are drawn at (the `wght` axis of the icon font): the system's weight for a control's own mark, heavier than its icons in the default system. The glyph box (mark.size) does not change with it; only the stroke does.

width.$description: The stroke of the check and the dash drawn as paths. No behaviour of the current spec reads it: the mark is a glyph of the icon set (CHK-12). It stays only so that the platforms that still draw them as paths keep building; remove it in the commit that brings the last of them up to date.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

mark-enter-scale.$description: The size the glyph grows from when it appears, and shrinks to when it goes, as a fraction of mark.size, about the box's center. 1 fades without growing.

mark-scale-duration.$description: How long the glyph takes to grow in from, or shrink out to, mark-enter-scale when the condition changes.

mark-scale-easing.$description: The curve of the glyph's scale. A size may overshoot and settle; this is a spatial curve.

selection-duration.$description: How long the box, outline and glyph take to change color, and the glyph to fade in or out, when the condition changes.

selection-easing.$description: The curve of the colors and the glyph's opacity. An opacity or a color cannot overshoot, so this is an effects curve.

width.$description: The border of the box, drawn inside its edge; the fill sits inside the border and never under it. 2.

weight.$description: The weight a selected filter chip's check is drawn at (the `wght` axis of the icon font): the system's weight for a control's own mark, as the checkbox draws its own, because the check is drawn on the chip's selected fill only while it is on and is what tells on from off beside the fill's color. The check's box (icon.size) does not change with it; only the stroke does. The leading icon and the remove glyph keep sys.icon.weight.

shape.$description: The corner of the container, capped at half its height: sys.shape.corner.full makes the chip a pill at any height.

elevation.$description: The elevated chip's resting depth. Tanrei's level1 is only the hairline ring, which draws the same edge as the outlined chip, so it rests at level2; a system whose level1 is a real shadow (m3-like, cupertino) sets level1.

color.$description: At rest a destructive remove glyph looks like any other; the default system turns it sys.color.error while it is hovered, focused or pressed (a rule).
The color hover, focus and press of a destructive remove action mix into its round container: the error role.
The color hover, focus and press of the remove action mix into its own round container.

elevation.$description: As the elevated chip's resting depth: level2 here, level1 in a system whose level1 is a real shadow.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press mix into the container: the label color.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

selection-duration.$description: How long a filter chip takes to show or hide its check (the chip's width changes with it) and to change to or from the selected look.

color.$description: At rest a destructive remove glyph looks like any other; the default system turns it sys.color.error while it is hovered, focused or pressed (a rule).
The color hover, focus and press of a destructive remove action mix into its round container: the error role.

The edge of an outlined chip at rest. In the default system it is the hairline role, the color the divider draws its line in. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw the edge apart from its dividers.
The color hover, focus and press of the remove action mix into its own round container.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container: the label color.
The color of code that carries no syntax role, and of all code that is not highlighted.

tab-size.$description: How many columns of the code face a tab character advances to the next multiple of.

shape.$description: The block's corners.

inset.$description: The distance of the copy button from the block's top edge and from its end edge. With the medium size's padding it centres a small button on the first line of code, so a block of one line holds the button without growing.

color.$description: The filled look's fill: a quiet step off the page. Every text color of the block is read on it.

gap.$description: Space between the header's items: the title, the language and the copy button.

padding-block-end.$description: Space between the header's row and the first line of code.

color.$description: The language label's color: quieter than the title, which it may stand beside.

typescale.$description: The language label's text style.

color.$description: The line numbers' color. They are set in the code's own text style, with digits of one width.

gap.$description: Space between the gutter (the bar's column, the numbers and the signs) and the start of the code.

color.$description: The band behind an added line, from the block's left edge to its right: a faint tint of the success color, so that the line reads as added at a glance whatever the colors of its code. Its code keeps its syntax colors, held on this band at the code's contrast. Never the only mark: the bar and the plus sign are drawn with it, and in forced colors the band is not drawn.
The bar and the plus sign of an added line.

The band behind a highlighted line, from the block's left edge to its right. Decorative: the bar marks the line where the band cannot be seen (an outlined block on a surface of the same tone, forced colors).
The bar of a highlighted line: the color of the one that is chosen.

width.$description: The width of the bar drawn at the left edge of a highlighted, an added or a removed line.

color.$description: The band behind a removed line, from the block's left edge to its right: a faint tint of the error color, so that the line reads as removed at a glance whatever the colors of its code. Its code keeps its syntax colors, held on this band at the code's contrast. Never the only mark: the bar and the minus sign are drawn with it, and in forced colors the band is not drawn.
The bar and the minus sign of a removed line.
The outlined look's edge: the system's one hairline. Decorative: the face and the padding set the code apart without it.

width.$description: The width of the outlined look's edge, drawn inside the block's size. The filled look draws no edge.

color.$description: The outlined look's fill: none. The code is read on the surface the block is placed on.
The color of the prompt drawn before each line of a block of commands.

comment.$description: Comments and documentation comments: what the code's author says about the code. Quieter than the code, and without a hue.

constant.$description: Values that are not text: numbers, booleans and null, named constants, units, color values, escapes. The code's color here; the default system gives it an orange.

function.$description: The name of a function or a method, where it is declared and where it is called. The code's color here; the default system gives it a blue.

keyword.$description: The language's own words: keywords, storage and modifier words, at-rules, annotations. The code's color here, told by weight; the default system gives it a purple as well.

property.$description: A name that belongs to something: a property, a key of an object or of a data file, an attribute of markup, a declaration's property in a style sheet, an option of a command. The code's color here; the default system gives it the blue of a function's name at a tone nearer the text.

punctuation.$description: Brackets, separators and the delimiters of markup: quieter than the words they hold together. Operators are not punctuation: they stay the code's color.

string.$description: Text written in the code: strings, characters, regular expressions, the values of markup attributes, the text of a template. The code's color here; the default system gives it a green, from a palette that is syntax's own and not the success color.

tag.$description: What markup and style sheets address: an element's name, a component's name in markup, a selector. The code's color here; the default system gives it a red, from a palette that is syntax's own and not the error color.

type.$description: The name of a type: a class, a structure, an interface, an enumeration, a built-in type, a namespace. The code's color here; the default system gives it a blue-green.

constant.$description: The weight a constant gains: none.

function.$description: The weight a function gains: none.

keyword.$description: Keywords gain the amount strong text gains in running text: they are told by weight before they are told by color, so they are still told where color is not seen.

property.$description: The weight a property gains: none.

string.$description: The weight a string gains: none.

tag.$description: The weight a tag gains: none.

type.$description: The weight a type gains: none.

max-length.$description: The longest code, in characters, that the block highlights by itself. Longer code is drawn plain: a run is a piece of the document on every platform, and a file of many thousands of lines is read in an editor, not in a page.

color.$description: The title's color.

typescale.$description: The title's text style. A product whose titles are always file names may set the small code role here.

color.$description: The swatch's edge, in every look and state: the one hairline, the color the divider draws its line in. It bounds a sample whose color is close to the container's, and it is all an empty swatch draws. Decorative: the value's text carries the meaning.

width.$description: The width of the swatch's edge, drawn inside its size, over the color.

shape.$description: The swatch's corners, never more than half its side: a slightly rounded square in the default system. A product that shows its colors as dots sets sys.shape.corner.full here.

action-gap.$description: Between the clear button and the chevron at the end of the container.

color.$description: The one hairline, between two groups under divider.

space.$description: Under divider: space above and below the line. Not read under gap.

padding-inline.$description: A title starts where the rows' content starts.

typescale.$description: The heading above a group's options.

gap.$description: Under gap: the empty space between two groups. Not read under divider.

color.$description: The list's surface: the raised sheet a menu, a select's list and a popover are drawn on.

max-height.$description: The tallest the list grows before its rows scroll: six rows and most of a seventh at the default row height, so that a cut row shows there is more. The room left in the window limits it further.

offset.$description: Distance between the container and the list.

padding-block.$description: Inset above the first row and below the last.

padding-inline.$description: Inset at the sides of the rows. With an option's own padding it puts an option's label under the text in the input.

shape.$description: The list's corners.

viewport-margin.$description: The least distance the list keeps from the window's edges and from an on-screen keyboard.

close-duration.$description: How long the list takes to go.

feedback-duration.$description: How long an option's ripple takes to grow.

open-duration.$description: How long the list takes to appear.

state-duration.$description: How long colors and edge widths take to follow a change of state.

gap.$description: Distance between a row's glyph, its text and its check.

height.$description: Minimum height of an option's row; the row grows with its text.

typescale.$description: An option's label.

size.$description: The glyph before an option's label.
The check at the end of the chosen option's row, and the box kept for it in every row.

emphasis.$description: How much weight the part of an option's label that matched the typed text gains, added to the weight of option.label.typescale. Weight alone: a match is not a selection, a choice or a link, so it takes no color.

padding-block.$description: Padding above and below a row's text; also above and below a group's title and the status row.

padding-inline.$description: Padding at each end of a row.

shape.$description: The corners of a row's highlight and of its state layer.

typescale.$description: The line under an option's label.

separation.$description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color, with divider.space above and below it. gap: group.gap of empty space and no line. Follows the system's choice; a combobox's separation prop overrides it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The status row's text while nothing is wrong, and the text shown when nothing matches: secondary to the options.
The status row's text while status is error. The words say what failed; the color says that something did.

typescale.$description: The status row's text and the text shown when nothing matches.

duration.$description: How long the button shows the copied or the failed form before it returns to rest: long enough to be seen by someone looking at where the text will be pasted, short enough that a second copy a moment later is confirmed anew.

resize-duration.$description: How long the label's box takes to change its width to the text now shown, while labelWidth is fit (CPY-19). Unused while labelWidth is widest; at once where motion is reduced.

arrangement.$description: How Cancel and OK sit. fill: a full-width Button group, the two sharing the container's inner width equally. end: at their own widths, aligned to the end. Either stacks into a column when the row does not fit. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between Cancel and OK, in a row or stacked. At sys.target.touch minus the lowest Button (small, 32) or more, each keeps its whole target in a column, as the dialog's actions do.

padding-block.$description: Above and below the actions.

variant.$description: The Button variant of Cancel and OK. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between the calendar and the time section, stacked or side by side, and between the rows of the time section (its tabs, the time display, the wheels or the dial).

padding-block.$description: Above the first section and below the last (above the actions when there are actions).

padding-inline.$description: The inset of the calendar, the time section, the error line and the actions from the surface's sides.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot at the dial's centre.

color.$description: The dial's face. surface-dim recedes from the surface in every scheme, where the tonal containers are within a step or two of surface-bright in the dark default.

size.$description: The diameter of the clock dial.
The diameter of the handle over the chosen value.

padding.$description: Between the dial's edge and the handle at the outer ring.

color.$description: The number under the handle, and the dot the handle holds between two numbers.
The line from the centre to the handle, and the centre dot.

offset.$description: The gap between the anchor and a docked picker.

viewport-margin.$description: How close a docked picker may come to the edges of the viewport before it flips or shifts.

typescale.$description: The line that says a range's end is before its start.

gap.$description: Between the title row and the chosen value below it.

padding-inline-end.$description: Smaller than the start, because the entry-mode tabs carry their own padding at the end of the title row.

color.$description: The part of the header's value that is not chosen yet ("Date", "End date").

typescale.$description: The chosen date, date and time, or range, in the header of a modal picker.

margin.$description: The least distance between a modal picker and the edges of the window's safe area and the on-screen keyboard.

enter-scale.$description: The size a modal picker grows from, as a fraction of its own, while it fades in. 1 fades without growing.

blur.$description: How much the scrim behind a modal picker blurs what lies behind it: the modal layer's, as a dialog's.

color.$description: The dim over everything behind a modal picker, alpha included: the modal layer's, as a dialog's.

dial-duration.$description: How long the dial takes to change from hours to minutes (and back), and the handle to travel to a value set from a selector.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

wheel-duration.$description: How long a wheel takes to settle on a value after a drag, a press on a row or a key, when it is not already moving with a fling.

width.$description: The least width of the period: the period wheel in the wheels mode and the period selector in the dial mode. Narrower than the hour's and the minute's boxes, and wider than the touch target, because it takes a press; it grows for a longer name. Its height is the selectors' in the dial mode and a wheel row's in the wheels mode.

gap.$description: Between the period and the hour and minute it qualifies: after the minute, or before the hour where the locale writes the period first. Wider than the gap around the separator, so that the hour and the minute read as one number pair and the period as its suffix.

typescale.$description: The name of the period (AM, PM) in the period wheel and the period selector. The range fields' step: well below the selectors' and the wheels' digits, so that the period reads as a qualifier of the time.

height.$description: The least height of a range field, one end of a span of times in the range display. The touch target, because a press on it chooses which end the wheels or the dial set.

padding-inline.$description: Between a range field's edge and its time, at each end.

gap.$description: Between a range field and the dash.

typescale.$description: The time in a range field, and the dash between the two. Two steps below the wheels' values: the range display says what is being set, the wheels or the dial set it.

color.$description: The edge of the selector whose unit the dial shows: the selector being set is marked as a focused field is, by its edge.

height.$description: The least height of the hour and minute selectors.

shape.$description: The corners of the hour and minute selectors, and of the range fields, which are selectors of an end.

width.$description: The width of the hour and the minute selector in the dial mode.

gap.$description: Between a selector and the separator.

typescale.$description: The hour and the minute in the selectors.

color.$description: The separator between the hour and the minute, and the dash between the two range fields: the marks that join two values.

typescale.$description: The separator between the selectors. Between the wheels it takes the wheels' text style, and the dash between the range fields takes theirs.

entry-modes.$description: Which ways of setting a time the picker offers. both: wheels and dial, chosen by two icon-only tabs; wheels: wheels only; dial: dial only. With one, no entry-mode tabs are drawn and entryMode is ignored. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between a wheel and the separator: the space that parts the two selection containers from the separator between them.

height.$description: The height of the wheels: five rows at the default row height, and the dial's diameter, so that switching between wheels and dial does not move the actions.

color.$description: The values above and below the selection band.

typescale.$description: The values on the wheels.

height.$description: The height of one value on a wheel. At least the minimum target: a press on a row above or below the middle moves it to the middle.

color.$description: The value on the selection band: the chosen one.

The ground behind a wheel's chosen value: one container for each wheel, or one band across both wheels and the separator where wheel.selection.span is joined. surface-dim recedes from the surface in every scheme, as the dial's face and the selectors do.

span.$description: Whether the wheels' chosen values stand on grounds of their own. each: one selection container behind each wheel's middle row, with the separator between the two, so that the hour and the minute read as two fields, as the dial mode's selectors do. joined: one container behind the middle row of both wheels and the separator, as a drum picker's band. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

width.$description: The width of the hour wheel and of the minute wheel.

gap.$description: The space between two columns of facts in the stacked and stat layouts. Larger than term.gap and stack.gap, so that two facts side by side are not read as one.

min-width.$description: The least width of a column that holds values. A list in columns draws only as many columns as are at least this wide (DSL-7); an inline list whose value column would be narrower than this draws its terms above their values instead (DSL-4). It grows with enlarged text (DSL-21).

color.$description: The line between two facts: the system's one hairline color. Decorative: facts, terms and values are exposed without it.

thickness.$description: The width of the line between two facts.

separation.$description: How a fact is told from the fact below it. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color between them, with fact.gap on each side of it. gap: fact.gap of empty space and no line. Follows the system's choice; a list's separation prop overrides it (DSL-13). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: The space between a term and the value under it, between a figure and its label, and between two values of one term. Small, so that a term and its values read as one fact.

color.$description: The text of a term, and of a figure's label in the stat layout: secondary content, quieter than the value it names.
The text of a value, and of a figure in the stat layout.

arrangement.$description: How the actions sit. fill: a full-width Button group, the actions sharing the container's inner width equally. end: at their own widths, aligned to the end. Either stacks into a column when the row does not fit (DLG-10). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between two actions, in a row or stacked. At sys.target.touch minus the lowest Button (small, 32) or more, every action keeps its whole target in a column, as comp.button-group.standard.gap does.

margin-block-start.$description: Between the last of the header, text and content and the actions.

variant.$description: The Button variant the dialog gives an action whose variant the product did not set (DLG-20). An action whose variant is set keeps it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

window-width.$description: A window narrower than this is compact: the dialog sits at the bottom of it instead of its centre (DLG-17). 0 keeps the dialog centred in every window.

gap.$description: Between the header, the supporting text and the content, top to bottom, and between the icon and the headline when the icon sits above it.

margin.$description: The least distance between the container and the edges of the window's safe area (and the on-screen keyboard), centred or at the bottom. It wins over min-width on a narrow window.

max-width.$description: The widest a dialog draws, centred or at the bottom; longer text wraps and wider content scrolls or wraps.

min-width.$description: The narrowest a dialog draws, unless the window less its margins is narrower.

padding.$description: The inset of the header, text, content and actions from the container's edges, on every side.

shape.$description: Every corner of the container, centred or at the bottom of a compact window.

color.$description: The foreground the dialog hands to its custom content (a list, a field's surroundings), as the platform's inherited color.

gap.$description: Between the icon and the headline beside it, while the icon sits at the headline's start (icon.placement inline).

placement.$description: Where the icon sits. inline: at the start of the headline's first line, header.gap before it, the headline and the supporting text aligned to the start. above: above the headline, container.gap apart, the icon and the headline centred and the supporting text at the start. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

enter-offset.$description: How far below its place a container at the bottom of a compact window starts as it rises in, and sinks as it leaves. 0 fades without moving.

enter-scale.$description: The size a centred container grows from, as a fraction of its own, while it fades in. 1 fades without growing.

blur.$description: How much the scrim behind the dialog blurs what lies behind it: the modal layer's (0, none, in the default system).

color.$description: The dim over everything behind the dialog, alpha included: the modal layer's, unless a system sets the dialog apart.

gap.$description: The least space between two dashes, from one dash's edge to the next. The divider widens the gaps equally so that a whole dash ends the line at each end.

length.$description: The length of one dash of a dashed line, round caps included. A dash is never drawn shorter than the line is thick.

gap.$description: The least space between two dots of a dotted line, from one dot's edge to the next. A dot is as long as the line is thick. The divider widens the gaps equally so that a whole dot ends the line at each end.

inset.$description: How far the line is shortened at its start (inset start) or at both ends (inset both): the inline-start of a horizontal divider, the top of a vertical one. A divider's insetLength replaces it for that divider.

thickness.$description: The line's extent across its axis: the side of a dot, the width of a dash, the width of the wave's stroke.

amplitude.$description: How far the wave's crest lies from the line's midline, measured to the center of the stroke. The divider takes twice this plus line.thickness across its axis. 0 draws a straight line.

wavelength.$description: The length of one whole wave, a crest and a trough. The divider stretches or shrinks it so that a whole number of waves fills the line.

color.$description: The glyph while the zone will take what is dragged over it: the color of its edge.

size.$description: The glyph above the message: the largest step of the icon scale, as the File picker's drop area's.

color.$description: The message on the panel: the surface's text color.

typescale.$description: The message: running text one step larger than the interface's, because it is read at a glance during a drag.

duration.$description: How long the overlay takes to fade in when a drag of files enters the zone, and to fade out when it leaves, ends or drops; and how long a change between taking and refusing takes.

color.$description: That edge while the zone will take what is dragged over it.

width.$description: The edge drawn inside the zone's box while files are dragged over it: the heavier stroke, the mark of what is selected, because the whole zone is the place now chosen.

color.$description: The panel that holds the glyph and the message, over the scrim: a raised surface, so that the message is read on its own ground whatever content lies under the scrim.

elevation.$description: The panel's lift over the scrim.

gap.$description: The space between the glyph and the message.

margin.$description: The least distance between the panel and the zone's edges: the panel never touches the edge, and never leaves the zone.

max-width.$description: The widest the panel draws; a longer message wraps. A narrower zone gives the panel its own width less panel.margin on each side.

padding-block.$description: The room above the glyph and below the message.

padding-inline.$description: The room at the panel's start and end.

shape.$description: Every corner of the panel: the step of a surface raised over the content, as a dialog's.

color.$description: The glyph, which becomes the icon set's block glyph, in the same role.
The edge while the zone will not take what is dragged over it: the error role, because letting go here fails.
The dim over the zone's content while files are dragged over it, alpha included (the scrim role is the overlay as drawn): the content is still there, and not what is pointed at now.

typescale.$description: The typed text and the placeholder. One line of it is the unit minRows and maxRows count in. 16 px, so that a touch browser does not zoom into the input.

resize-duration.$description: How long the height takes to change when the number of lines shown changes (ETI-8).

color.$description: The highlight behind selected text, in every state. Selected text is the one that is chosen now, and the system marks that with a primary fill under on-primary content wherever it appears. Pair: selection.content.color.
The text on the highlight. A layer whose highlight is a tint that keeps the typed text readable sets this to the text's color.
The insertion point: the one thing the input itself shows of having focus. It is not the focus indication, which is the holder's.
The typed text.
The hint in the empty input.

gap.$description: The space between the text and the row of actions.

item-gap.$description: The space between two actions, in the row and between rows when the actions wrap.

padding-inline.$description: The room at the start and the end: the inset a card, a callout and a list row give their content in the default system, so a start-aligned empty state begins where the rows would have.

measure.$description: The longest line of the title and of the description, as a multiple of the description's font size (ems): about 60 characters of Latin text, 30 of Japanese or Chinese. A short message in the middle of a wide table would otherwise run in one long line from edge to edge.

color.$description: The description's color: secondary content, quieter than the title.
The glyph's color: secondary content. Decorative: the title says what the glyph pictures.

gap.$description: The space between the glyph or the picture and the title.

color.$description: The title's color: the surface's text color. The one part of an empty state at full strength, so that it is what a reader sees first.

gap.$description: The space between the title and the description.

shape-open.$description: The open toggle's corners: round, so that it reads as a close button rather than the action it was.

color.$description: The toggle's fill while closed.
The toggle's glyph while closed.
An item's fill.
The color hover, focus and press mix into an item: its label color.
The toggle's fill while open.
The close glyph's color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the open toggle: its icon color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the closed toggle: its icon color.

gap.$description: Space between the icon and the label.

height.$description: An item's minimum height.

shape.$description: An item's corners.

gap.$description: Space between two items.

offset.$description: Space between the lowest item and the toggle.

close-duration.$description: The items leaving together and the toggle changing back.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the ripple takes to spread.

open-duration.$description: The toggle's change and each item's entrance when the menu opens.

stagger.$description: The delay between one item's entrance and the next.

color.$description: The toggle's fill while closed.
The toggle's glyph while closed.
An item's fill.
The color hover, focus and press mix into an item: its label color.
The toggle's fill while open.
The close glyph's color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the open toggle: its icon color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the closed toggle: its icon color.
The toggle's fill while closed.
The toggle's glyph while closed.
An item's fill.
The color hover, focus and press mix into an item: its label color.
The toggle's fill while open.
The close glyph's color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the open toggle: its icon color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the closed toggle: its icon color.

gap.$description: Distance between the last control and the error text: a field's distance between its control and its supporting row.

min-width.$description: The least width of a field in a horizontal row of fields (FGR-13): the fields share the row equally and never less than this, and a field that would be narrower moves, with those after it, to the next line. A field whose content needs more keeps what its content needs.

gap-inline.$description: Distance between two members that stand side by side in a horizontal group: from the end of one control's label to the next control, wide enough that a label is read with its own mark and not with the next one; and between two fields in one row (a city and its postal code).

controls.$description: Between two selection controls: with their 40 containers it puts their marks 48 apart, so that each keeps a whole touch target of its own.

fields.$description: Between two fields: wider than any distance inside one field (8 under the label, 4 above the help), so that each field's label, control and help read as one block. Also the distance between two fields of a form outside any group.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's last line, or the description's where there is one, and the first control: a field's distance between its label and its control.

typescale.$description: The group's label: the style of a field's label, because it does the same work for a set.

asterisk-gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the asterisk: it belongs to the word it follows, closer than a tag stands.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the requirement tag: where the tag stands is the frame's; what the tag looks like is the Tag's (comp.tag.*).

mark.$description: How a required set is marked beside its label when the set does not say (FGR-6). tag: a small filled Tag holding requiredText. asterisk: "*" after the label. none: no mark; the requirement is still exposed. Follows the system's choice, as the Field's comp.field.requirement.mark does; a set's requiredMark prop overrides it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The group's error text, below its controls: the error role, used for errors and nothing else.
The label keeps naming the set while it is in error; the error text and the controls themselves show the error.
The description stays as it is in error: it says how to answer, which is what the person needs now.
The label: the surface's text color, stronger than the supporting text, because it names the set.
The asterisk of a required mark drawn as an asterisk: primary, the role a filled tag is drawn in, never the error color, because nothing is wrong yet.
The description under the label: secondary text.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's last line and the description: the two are read as one heading for the set.

typescale.$description: The description and the error text.

gap.$description: The least distance between the help or the error text and the count at the end of the row's first line.

Distance between the help's last line and the error text below it, while the field shows both — under error-text.placement append: the frame's distance between two rows of small text, the one a field group keeps between its label and its description. A field without help, and every field under replace, has its error text supporting-text.gap below the control, and this token is not read.

placement.$description: Where the error text stands while the field is in error and has words for it (FLD-7, FLD-31). replace: in the help's place — the help is not drawn, and the error text is the supporting row's first line, supporting-text.gap below the control. append: below the help, which stays, error-text.gap from its last line. A field without help draws its error text in the same place under both. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Distance between the label glyph and the label.

size.$description: The glyph before the label: the icon scale's small step, one line of the label high.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's last line and the control.

typescale.$description: The label above the control: the text field's label style, so that a framed control and a text field in one form are named alike.

state-duration.$description: How long a change of the frame's colors takes when focus enters or leaves, or the error or disabled condition changes: the text field's state duration.

asterisk-gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the asterisk: it belongs to the word it follows, closer than a tag stands.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the requirement tag: where the tag stands is the frame's; what the tag looks like is the Tag's (comp.tag.*).

mark.$description: How a required control is marked beside its label when the field does not say (FLD-6). tag: a small filled Tag holding requiredText. asterisk: "*" after the label. none: no mark; the requirement is still exposed. Follows the system's choice; a field's requiredMark prop overrides it. A text field is this field around a text input, and a label that floats in the input shows tag as an asterisk (FLD-25). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The count the field is given (countText: a text input's characters typed and the limit): secondary text, as the help is.
The error text, below the help or directly below the control: the error role, used for errors and nothing else. The same id, with the same value, as a field group's.
The count while the field is in error: unchanged. The error text takes the error color; the count does not.
The label keeps naming the control while it is in error; the error text and the control itself show the error.
The help while the field is in error: unchanged, as a field group's description. It says how to answer, which is what the person needs now; the error text below it takes the error color.
The value text keeps its color while the field is in error: the error text alone takes the error color.
The glyph before the label: one step quieter than the label it accompanies.
The label: the surface's text color, stronger than the supporting text, because it names the control.
The asterisk of a required mark drawn as an asterisk: primary, the role a filled tag is drawn in, never the error color, because nothing is wrong yet.
The help: secondary text.
The value text: quieter than the label, which names the control, and as strong as the help, which it reads like.
