gap.$description: From the container to the label. With the 40 container it starts the label where the 48 target ends.

typescale.$description: The visible label.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

selection-duration.$description: How long the ring's stroke takes to thicken or thin, and the ring and fill to change color (the fill from none to its color and back), when the selection changes.

min-height.$description: The least height one option takes in layout, the container centered in it. At the target size, options stacked with no space between them keep whole targets that do not overlap; a layer may lower it, accepting shared target area, or raise it.

selected-width-share.$description: The stroke of the selected ring, as a share of the ring's radius, drawn inward from the outer diameter: 0 keeps ring.width, 1 is a stroke as wide as the radius (a solid disc). A share narrower than ring.width draws ring.width.

size.$description: The outer diameter of the ring, the same in both conditions, 20.

width.$description: The stroke of the unselected ring, drawn inside its outer diameter. It is also the thinnest the selected ring's stroke can be.

color.$description: The fill inside the selected ring, drawn at fill.opacity.
The fill's color while unselected, where the selection motion starts and ends it: none in the default system, so an unselected radio button shows no fill.

button-gap.$description: Between two neighbouring action buttons of the bar: the clear button and the icon-only Buttons of the trailing slot. 0 in the default system: the buttons stand as close as their targets allow, each keeping sys.target.touch along the row (SRC-34), so two medium buttons (40) stand 8 apart and two that are 48 or wider touch.

gap.$description: Between the bar's elements (glyph or leading button, input, the first action button) and the full-screen header's (back button, input, clear button). Neighbouring hit areas meet at the middle of it (SRC-25), so it is what keeps an icon button's target whole on the side where it meets the input: at sys.target.touch minus a button's width or more, the button keeps its full target there. The default system's 16 is 48 minus the narrowest button there (the bar's small clear button, 32). The action buttons stand button-gap from one another instead.

height.$description: The bar's minimum height: Button's large and the large text field's, so a search bar shares a row with them.

padding-inline.$description: From the bar's start edge to the search glyph, and from its end edge to the input or the clear button.

padding-inline-with-button.$description: From the bar's edge to an icon button in the leading or trailing slot, or to the clear button at the end. Where an icon button's hit area stops at the bar's edge, this is what gives it its whole target on that side: at least half of sys.target.touch minus the button's width. The default system's 8 is half of 48 minus the narrowest button there (the small clear button, 32).

color.$description: The line under the full-screen header.
A group title is quieter than the results under it.

typescale.$description: The heading of a group without a destination ("Pages").

gap.$description: Above and below a result group, between it and its neighbours in the view.

indent.$description: How far the results of a group with a linked heading are inset at the start, so that they read as its parts.

height.$description: The full-screen view's top row (back button, input, clear button): the small app bar's height.

padding-inline.$description: From the window's edges to the back button and the header's last element: the app bar's inset.

typescale.$description: The value and the placeholder, in the bar and in the full-screen header. 16 px, so iOS Safari does not zoom into it.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the ripple takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple.

width.$description: The bar's edge at rest; its focused width is a state token.

color.$description: The text of a match inside an excerpt: the stronger of the two text colors, against the excerpt's on-surface-variant. No hue: a match is not a selection, a choice or a link.

The fill behind a match, as well as its weight and color: the quiet tonal container, so that a match is found in every script, also where the reader's font has no weight between regular and bold and the raised weight draws as the regular one. result.mark.color is read on it at the text ratio in every scheme.

emphasis.$description: How much weight a match gains over the excerpt's text, added to the excerpt typescale's weight.

color.$description: The legends' color: as quiet as the placeholder they stand beside.

typescale.$description: The legends of the shortcut hint, in the trigger and in the bar (SRC-37). The caps are the keyboard shortcut's own.

color.$description: The bar's fill: the filled text field's.

elevation.$description: The bar's lift: none in Tanrei; a bar that floats over a map or an image is raised.

color.$description: The search glyph at the bar's start.
The color hover and press mix into the bar: its input color, as the filled text field's.
The color hover, the active highlight and press mix into a suggestion row: its headline color.
The status row's text while nothing is wrong.
The status row's text while status is error. The words say what failed; the color says that something did.

typescale.$description: The status row's text: the count, or that nothing was found.

gap.$description: Between a suggestion's leading icon and its text.

height.$description: A suggestion row's minimum height: the menu item's.

shape.$description: The corners of a suggestion's highlight, inset in the view by its padding.

gap.$description: Between the trigger's glyph, text and shortcut hint. Nothing in the trigger is a button of its own, so no target depends on it, unlike the bar's gap.

height.$description: The button trigger's minimum height: Button's medium, so that it shares an app bar's row with the icon-only Buttons beside it. Its hit area is extended to the minimum target (SRC-36).

padding-inline.$description: From the trigger's start edge to the search glyph, and from its end edge to the shortcut hint or the text.

typescale.$description: The trigger's text (the placeholder, or the label). Not an input: the 16 px floor that keeps iOS Safari from zooming does not apply.

size.$description: The search glyph in the button trigger: a medium Button's glyph.

color.$description: The view's surface, docked under the bar or over the whole window.

elevation.$description: The docked view's lift. A full-screen view covers the window, so no edge of it shows.

shape.$description: The docked view's corners. A full-screen view fills the window with none.

max-width.$description: The widest the dialog view draws; a narrower window gets a narrower view (SRC-40). Wide enough for an excerpt line of about 80 characters.

offset.$description: From the top of the window's safe area to the dialog view. The view hangs from the top instead of being centered, so that the input stays where it is while the results under it come and go.
Between the bar and the docked view.

blur.$description: How much the scrim behind the dialog view blurs what lies behind it: the modal layer's, as the dialog's.

color.$description: The dim over everything behind the dialog view, alpha included: the modal layer's, as the dialog's.

viewport-margin.$description: How close the docked view may come to the viewport's edge or the on-screen keyboard.

weight.$description: The weight the check of a selected segment is drawn at (the `wght` axis of the icon font): the system's weight for a control's own mark, as the checkbox draws its own, because the check is a thin stroke drawn on the segment's selected fill and is what tells selected from unselected beside the fill's color. The check's box (check.size) does not change with it; only the stroke does. A segment's icon keeps sys.icon.weight.

shape.$description: The corners where a segment meets its neighbours (the outer corners of the end segments follow set.shape).

color.$description: The line between two segments, the same as the outline by default so the set reads as one outlined shape cut into segments.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the ripple takes to spread.

selection-duration.$description: The check appearing or leaving and the segment changing to or from the selected colors.

color.$description: The border around the set: a functional 3:1 boundary, as an outlined button's.
The icon, and the check of a selected segment.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the segment: its label color.
The fill behind the segments.

padding.$description: The inset of the segments from the set's edge: 0 joins them to the outline; a system whose selection floats inside a track insets them.

shape.$description: The set's outer corners, and so the first and last segments' outer corners.

color.$description: The icon, and the check of a selected segment.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the segment: its label color.
The one hairline, between two groups while separation is divider.

space.$description: Space above and below the divider.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of a group's heading from the rows' edges.

typescale.$description: A group's heading.

gap.$description: The space between two groups while separation is gap.

color.$description: The list's surface: the raised sheet a menu and a popover are drawn on.

max-height.$description: The tallest the list grows before its options scroll: six rows and most of a seventh at the default row height, so that a cut row shows there is more. The room left in the window limits it further.

max-width.$description: The widest the list grows for its options where its trigger is narrower: an option that needs more wraps. A list is never narrower than its trigger, so a trigger wider than this gives the list its own width. The window limits it further.

min-width.$description: The least width of the list where its options and its trigger are narrower than this (a small select in a bar).

offset.$description: Distance between the trigger and its list.

padding-block.$description: Inset above the first option and below the last.

padding-inline.$description: Inset at the sides of the options. With an option's own padding it puts an option's label under the value the trigger shows.

shape.$description: The list's corners.

viewport-margin.$description: How close the list may come to the window's edge.

close-duration.$description: How long the list takes to go.

feedback-duration.$description: How long a ripple takes to grow over a pressed option.

open-duration.$description: How long the list takes to appear.

state-duration.$description: How long a change of colors and edge widths takes.

gap.$description: Distance between an option's glyph, its text and its check.

height.$description: An option's minimum height.

typescale.$description: An option's label.

size.$description: An option's glyph.
The box of the check at the end of the chosen option's row, kept in every row so that labels wrap alike.

padding-block.$description: Padding above and below an option's content.

padding-inline.$description: Padding at the sides of an option's row.

shape.$description: The corners of an option's row.

typescale.$description: The line below an option's label.

separation.$description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: divider or gap. Follows the system's choice; a select's separation prop overrides it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

arrangement.$description: How the actions sit. fill: a full-width Button group, the actions sharing the sheet's inner width equally. start: at their own widths, the row aligned to the start edge. Either stacks into a column when the row does not fit (SSH-11). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Between two actions, in a row or stacked. At sys.target.touch minus the lowest Button (small, 32) or more, every action keeps its whole target in a column, as comp.button-group.standard.gap and comp.dialog.actions.gap do.

padding-block.$description: Above and below the row of actions, between the divider and the sheet's bottom edge.

variant.$description: The Button variant the sheet gives an action whose variant the product did not set (SSH-17). An action whose variant is set keeps it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.
The Button variant of the close button, an icon-only medium Button (SSH-5). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

modal.$description: Tanrei's level1 is only the hairline ring, so a sheet raised over the content rests at level2 (as the modal drawer).

padding-block.$description: Above the content when there is no header, and below it when there are no actions.

padding-inline.$description: From the sheet's start and end edges to the headline, the content and the actions.

width.$description: The sheet's width, not counting the system inset at its end. A modal sheet on a narrow window gives way so that a strip of scrim stays pressable (SSH-7).

color.$description: The foreground the sheet hands to its content, as the platform's inherited color.
The hairline above the actions, drawn while there are actions, and the one below the header, drawn while the content is scrolled from its top (SSH-11, SSH-19).

gap.$description: Between the headline and the close button.

height.$description: The header row's minimum height; the headline and the close button are centred in it, and it grows with a headline that wraps.

padding-inline-end.$description: From the sheet's end edge to the close button: less than the content's inset, so that the close glyph lines up near the text column while its target stays whole.

enter-duration.$description: How long a sheet takes to slide in (and a modal sheet's scrim to fade in), or a standard sheet to open in the layout: the modal layer's, so that every modal surface of a product keeps one tempo.

exit-duration.$description: How long a sheet takes to slide out (and a modal sheet's scrim to fade out), or a standard sheet to close in the layout: the modal layer's, so that every modal surface of a product keeps one tempo.

blur.$description: How much the scrim behind a modal sheet blurs what lies behind it: the modal layer's (0, none, in the default system).

color.$description: The dim over everything behind a modal sheet, alpha included: the modal layer's, unless a system sets the side sheet apart.

gap.$description: The space between two placeholders that stand one under another directly in the skeleton. Placeholders inside a layout of the product's own are spaced by that layout. The lines of one text placeholder have no gap: they are the line boxes of its text style.

animation.$description: How a shown skeleton stirs, so that it reads as waiting and not as broken. pulse: every placeholder's fill dims and returns, all of them together. wave: the same dimming passes through the skeleton from its start edge to its end edge, as one band across all of its placeholders. none: the placeholders are still. Under reduced motion every manner is drawn as none. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dim-duration.$description: How long the fill takes to fall from its resting opacity to its dim opacity; the way back takes as long, so one whole pulse, and one whole wave across the skeleton, is twice this.

dim-easing.$description: The curve of the fall and of the way back.

show-delay.$description: How long the skeleton waits, from the moment it is inserted, before it is drawn and exposed to assistive technology, so that a wait shorter than this shows the place blank instead of shapes that flash. Its box is kept during the wait.

color.$description: A placeholder's fill: the low-emphasis fill a track has, quiet enough that a view full of placeholders is not louder than the content that replaces them. Decorative: the wait is said by the skeleton's label, not by this color.

dim-opacity.$description: The opacity a placeholder's fill falls to at the low point of a pulse or in the trough of a wave, as a fraction of its resting opacity. 1 leaves the fill still under either manner.

last-line-inline-size.$description: How much of the last line of a text placeholder of two or more lines is drawn, as a fraction of the placeholder's inline size, from the start edge: a paragraph seldom ends at the edge, and a ragged end is what makes a stack of bars read as text. 1 draws every line whole.

block.$description: The corners of a block: the corners a card and a picture in content have in the default system.

circle.$description: The corners of a circle: the whole of them.

text.$description: The corners of each line of a text placeholder: barely eased, as a run of letters has no corners of its own.

size.$description: The diameter of the round state layer centered on each handle. It sets how far the track is inset from the slider's ends, so that a handle and its state layer stay inside the slider at min and max. 0 draws no state layer.

width.$description: The width of the handle's outline, drawn over its fill inside the handle's edge, so the handle keeps its width and height: a wider outline grows inward. Three stroke units in Tanrei, one more than sys.border.thick: on a 20 handle a 2 ring reads thin beside the track it ends, and 3 leaves a 14 disc of fill, still clearly a ring. 0 draws no outline.

shape.$description: The handle's corners, clamped to half its smaller side.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the ripple takes to spread from the handle's center when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple.

value-duration.$description: How long the handle takes to reach a value set by a key, assistive technology, a tap on the track or the product. A drag follows the press without it.

color.$description: A stop dot that lies on the active track.

width.$description: The handle's extent along the track. Equal to handle.height in Tanrei, so the handle is round.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press mix into the container: the handle's outline color. The fill is the surface's color in Tanrei and would not show on it.

height.$description: The value indicator's minimum height; it is never narrower than it is high.

offset.$description: Between the handle's outer edge across the track (the top of a round handle, its outline included) and the value indicator.

inverse.$description: Whether a snackbar whose inverse the product did not set is drawn inverse (SNK-30). off: on a surface of the scheme, from the unprefixed and the status tokens. on: in the opposite scheme's colors, from the inverse tokens. margin.$description: The least distance between the snackbar and the edges of its host's safe area (and the on-screen keyboard).

max-width.$description: The widest a snackbar draws on a large window; a longer message wraps.

min-height.$description: A minimum: the bar grows with a wrapped message, an action on its own row, or enlarged text.

min-width.$description: The narrowest a snackbar draws, so that a one-word message still reads as a bar. Never wider than the host less the margins.

padding-block.$description: Above and below the message. Heights are minimums, so this shows when the message wraps.

padding-inline-end.$description: After the message, when the snackbar has no action and no close button.

padding-inline-end-with-controls.$description: After the last control. Tighter than the text padding, because a control's own padding already surrounds its label or icon.

shape.$description: The bar's corners: the step of the rich tooltip and the card, one above a menu's, so that a bar holding pill controls does not read as a box.

gap.$description: Between the action, the expand button and the close button.

height.$description: The height of the action and the side of the close and expand buttons' squares: the three share a row. A minimum for the action, which grows with enlarged text. Every hit area meets the minimum target.

size.$description: The close and expand glyphs: an icon-only button's medium glyph.

padding-inline.$description: Before and after the action's label: a medium tonal Button's padding, since the action is drawn as one.

shape.$description: The corners of the action's container and of the close and expand buttons' state layers. Full in the default system: the action is a pill and an icon-only button a circle.

color.$description: The bar in the error form: a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, raised by the same elevation as the default form's. The default system values this role from the status's quiet palette, so the bar carries the hue and not its full chroma.
The focus indicator on the error bar: the bar's content color, which the invariants hold against the bar in every scheme.
The glyph takes the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet bar, drawn at icon.opacity. Its shape, not its color, tells the status apart (SNK-21).
The edge of the error bar: the status's own color, drawn at outline.opacity over the ring of the bar's elevation (SNK-31).
The outer stroke of the focus indicator on the default form's bar: the system's own, since that bar is a surface role the invariants hold it against.

gap.$description: Between the status glyph and the title or message after it.

opacity.$description: The opacity the status glyph is drawn at, applied to the glyph color of the form (SNK-21): a mark beside the text, a little softer than the text. Chosen so that the glyph keeps 3:1 against its bar in every status form and scheme of the default system.

size.$description: The status glyph (info, warning, error, check_circle). Drawn only in a status form.

opacity.$description: The opacity a status form's edge is drawn at, applied to the outline color of the form (SNK-31). 0 draws no edge of the status, so the elevation's ring shows as on the default form.

color.$description: The color of the compact form's position: secondary text.

gap.$description: The space between the compact form's bar and its position line.

typescale.$description: The text style of the compact form's position ("Step 2 of 5").

min-width.$description: The least width of a step's column in the horizontal form. Where the layout gives the stepper less than the number of steps times this, a horizontal stepper draws its compact form.

gap.$description: The space between two blocks of one step's body (a paragraph and the code block it introduces): what prose puts between the blocks nested in a list item in the default system, and half the space between two steps, so what belongs to one step is closer together than two steps are.

color.$description: The line that joins a marker to the next: the system's one hairline, the ring's color. Decorative.

gap.$description: The space the connector keeps from the marker above it and from the marker below it, so the line and the rings are read as separate marks.

thickness.$description: The connector's thickness. Zero draws no connector.

gap.$description: The space between the marker's column and the step's content. Every step's content begins at the same edge: the widest marker's width and this gap from the steps' start edge.

color.$description: The ring: the system's one hairline. Decorative — the number inside it is what is read — so it is not held to a contrast.

width.$description: The ring's width, drawn inside the marker's size.

padding-inline.$description: The least room between the marker's edge and its number at the start and the end. With it a number of one or two digits keeps the marker a circle in the default system; a longer one (a procedure continued at 100) widens it into a pill.

shape.$description: The marker's corners: a circle in the default system, and a pill where the number widens it. Never larger than half the marker's height.

gap.$description: The space between the end of one step and the beginning of the next: the space prose puts between two blocks in the default system, so a step is a block of the text it sits in, and twice the space between the blocks inside one step.
The space between a step's title and its body.

alternate-color.$description: The other color of the checkerboard, for every second square.

color.$description: One of the two colors of the checkerboard drawn under the color, which shows through a color that is not opaque and is covered by one that is.

size.$description: The side of one square of the checkerboard.

circle.$description: The corners of a circle sample: a dot.

square.$description: The corners of a square sample, never more than half its side: a slightly rounded square in the default system.

large.$description: The side of a large sample: where the color itself is looked at, in a palette or a theme’s overview.

medium.$description: The side of a medium sample: beside a line of body text, in a list row or a setting.

small.$description: The side of a small sample: beside one line of small text, in a table cell or a dense row.

large.$description: Between a large sample and its text.

medium.$description: Between a medium sample and its text.

small.$description: Between a small sample and its text.

color.$description: The color’s name, beside the sample.

The sample’s edge: the one hairline, the color the divider draws its line in. It bounds a sample whose color is close to the surface around it, and it is all an empty sample draws. The swatch’s text carries the meaning, so the edge is not held to a contrast ratio.

width.$description: The width of the sample’s edge, drawn inside its size, over the color.

color.$description: The line under the name: the color’s value, a token’s name, where it is used.

size.$description: The round state layer centered on the handle, 40; it moves with the handle and reaches 4 beyond the track's ends.

size-with-icon.$description: The smallest diameter of the handle while it shows an icon, 24; a larger size of the condition and state wins.

size.$description: The glyph box inside the handle: the icon set's glyph (check, close…) at a step of the icon scale, 16.

weight.$description: The weight the glyph in the handle is drawn at (the `wght` axis of the icon font), in both conditions: the system's weight for a control's own mark, heavier than its icons in the default system. The glyph box (icon.size) does not change with it; only the stroke does.

gap.$description: From the track to the label.

typescale.$description: The visible label.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

selection-duration.$description: How long the handle takes to travel along the track, and the track and handle to change color, when the switch changes.

width.$description: The border of the track, drawn inside its edge; the fill sits inside the border and never under it. 2.

size.$description: The diameter of the handle while on, 24. Its center stays on one line whatever the size: half the track height from the track's end.

height.$description: The height of the track, 32. The handle's center is half of it from the track's end.

width.$description: The length of the track, 52.

size.$description: The diameter of the handle while off, 16. Its center stays on one line whatever the size: half the track height from the track's end.

shape.$description: The corners of the region that holds the panels, below the Tab view's own row when it draws one. It clips a panel as it slides and blurs, and a focused panel's ring follows it. Square, because a Tab view usually spans the screen or its parent; a product that puts one inside a rounded surface rounds it.

fade-duration.$description: Where motion is reduced, how long the crossfade that replaces the switch takes.

fade-easing.$description: The reduced-motion crossfade's easing: an effects curve, which never overshoots.

switch-duration.$description: How long a switch takes when a tab is selected, and how long the rest of it takes after a swipe is released. The tabs' indicator slides over the same default, so the two land together.

switch-easing.$description: The switch's easing. A spatial spring may overshoot; the travel follows it, the fade and the blur stop at their end points.

transition.$description: The form a switch between two panels takes in a Tab view whose transition the product did not set (TBV-22). slide: the panels travel, fade and blur as transition.distance, transition.distance-fraction, transition.opacity and transition.blur say, over switch-duration, and follow a swipe. fade: the two panels crossfade in place over fade-duration, and crossfade with a swipe. none: the new panel is shown whole in the frame the selection is made, a swipe moves nothing before its release, and the row the view draws puts its indicator on the new tab at once. Reduced motion draws slide as fade and never adds motion to fade or none. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

blur.$description: How blurred a panel is at the fullest point of a switch: the standard deviation of the Gaussian, as the web's filter: blur() takes it. A platform whose blur takes another quantity converts; it never passes the number through. 0 draws no blur.

distance.$description: How far a panel travels between rest and the fullest point of a switch, before distance-fraction adds a share of the Tab view's width. The old panel moves this far toward the side it leaves by; the new one starts this far away on the other side.

distance-fraction.$description: The share of the Tab view's width added to distance: 0 keeps the travel at distance whatever the width; 1 (with distance 0) makes the panels travel a whole width, so that they move with the finger and meet edge to edge, as a page turn does.

opacity.$description: A panel's opacity at the fullest point of a switch: the old panel fades to it as it leaves, the new one fades from it as it arrives. 0 is a crossfade; 1 draws no fade.

color.$description: The fill of the compact form: its row and, when open, its list. A fill, because a compact table of contents is often kept over the text it describes.

shape.$description: The corners of the compact form.

color.$description: The chevron of the compact form's row.

size.$description: The chevron's box.

padding-block.$description: Below the open list, inside the compact form's fill.

padding-inline.$description: Between the compact form's edge and the open list's rail, and after its rows: the row's inline padding, so the rail stands under the title's first letter.

gap.$description: Between the title, the name of the current section and the chevron.

height.$description: The least height of the compact form's row: the touch target, because the compact form is the form of narrow windows. A minimum: it grows with enlarged text.

padding-inline.$description: Inside the compact form's row, before the title and after the chevron.

color.$description: The current section's name in the compact form's row: secondary text beside the title.

typescale.$description: The text style of the current section's name in the compact form's row: an item's.

gap.$description: Space between the title and the list.

color.$description: The fill of the current item's row. None: the quiet selection fill belongs to the product's navigation, and a fill that moves as the page scrolls would pull the eye from the text.
The current item: the color of the page's own text, because it names where the reader is.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the current row.
The fill of the compact form's row, over compact.container.color.
The title in the compact form's row.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the compact form's row.
The fill of an item's row. None at rest: it is where hover, focus and press are drawn.
An item that is not current: secondary text. The list is a quiet companion of the page, and its rows are told as links by being rows of a navigation list.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the row.

typescale.$description: The text style of every item, at every level: a step under the text the list describes, so that the list stays quieter than the page. The current item adds the system's emphasis for body text to its weight.

color.$description: The marker of the current item: primary, the one chosen now, as a tab's active indicator is. It is not the accent, which is keyboard focus alone.

width.$description: The thickness of the current item's marker on the rail: the heavier of the system's two strokes, so that it is told from the rail by its width as well as its color.

disclosure-duration.$description: How long the compact form takes to open or close: its list revealed or hidden, what follows moving, and its chevron turning. The name and the value of an accordion item's and of a navigation drawer group's.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

state-duration.$description: How long a state change of a row takes, and how long the marker and the weight of the current item take to change.

color.$description: The rail: the system's one hairline. It is the track the marker of the current item sits on. Decorative.

width.$description: The thickness of the line along the list's start edge.

indent.$description: How much further from the rail a label starts for each level of nesting. Only the label moves: the row, its state layer and its marker keep the list's full width.

padding-inline.$description: Inside a row: between the rail and a first-level label, and after every label. The same in both densities: density changes how tall a row is, not where its label starts.

shape.$description: The corners of a row's container, where hover, focus and press are drawn, and of the focus ring inside it.

color.$description: The title in the list presentation. In the compact form the title is the row's label and takes the row's label color.

typescale.$description: The text style of the title ("On this page"), in the list and in the compact form's row.

gap.$description: Space between the caption and the table's first row.

color.$description: The caption's text: secondary content.

typescale.$description: The caption's text style, at both densities: secondary text, one step under the regular cell's.

color.$description: The text of a cell, of a row header and of a footer cell.

The line between two rows, under the header row and above the footer rows; the line along the inner edge of a first column that is kept in view; and the line along an edge of the table's box beyond which there is more to scroll to. The system's one hairline color. Decorative: rows, headers and the scroll region are exposed without it.

thickness.$description: The width of every line the table draws.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below what stands in the place of the rows of a table that has none (the product's Empty state). Its inline space is a cell's, by density.

color.$description: The fill of the header row. None in the default system: a column header is told from the data by its text style, its quieter color and the line under it. A design system whose tables carry a filled header sets a container step here.

gap.$description: Space between the label of a sortable column's header and its mark.

size.$description: The glyph box of the mark of a sortable column, at both densities: the smallest step of the icon scale, beside a label.

weight.$description: The weight of the mark of a sortable column: it is the control's own mark, the one thing that says which way the rows run, drawn at the smallest size the system has; at the weight of an icon beside a label its stroke is about one pixel wide.

color.$description: The text of a column header: secondary content, quieter than the data it names.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press on a sortable header takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple: the pressed layer grows from the point of contact over this time, with state-easing. Unused by the other choices.

state-duration.$description: How long a sortable header takes to change between its states.

gap.$description: The empty space between two rows while separation is gap, in place of the line. Added to the cells' own block padding.

color.$description: The fill of a body row that is selected, across the row's whole width, in place of a stripe: the quiet selection, a selected list item's and a selected tree row's. A first column kept in view takes it over sticky.container.color.
The color hover and press mix into a chosen row (TBL-59): its text color, as a selected list item's and a selected tree row's.
The text of the cells and of the row header of a selected row. What a cell holds that is not plain text (a tag, a link, inline code) keeps its own colors.

The fill of a body row that can be chosen and is not, at rest: none of its own, so that its stripe, or the fill of a column kept in view, shows. Its hovered and pressed fills are laid over what shows (TBL-59).
The color hover and press mix into a row that can be chosen and is not (TBL-59): its text color.
The text of the cells of a body row that can be chosen and is not: a cell's own color.

separation.$description: How a row is told from the row next to it. divider: a line of divider.thickness in divider.color between them. gap: row.gap of empty space and no line. Follows the system's choice; a table's separation prop overrides it (TBL-9). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

color.$description: The fill of the header cell of a column that can be sorted and is not the one the rows are ordered by. None at rest: it is where hover, focus and press are drawn.
The mark that says the column can be sorted (the two-way arrow): secondary content.
The label of a sortable header that is not sorted: a column header's own color, so that a table whose columns can all be sorted reads as quietly as one whose columns cannot.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container.
The fill of the header cell of the column the rows are ordered by. None at rest.
The arrow that says which way the rows run: up for ascending, down for descending.
The label of the column the rows are ordered by: the color of the data, a step stronger than the other headers, so that the sorted column is told by more than its mark.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container.

gap.$description: Space between the status text and the pagination on one line, and between them when the line breaks in two.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the content of the status line. Its inline space is a cell's, by density, so that its text begins where the first column's does.

color.$description: The status text: secondary content, as the caption is.

typescale.$description: The status text, at both densities: the caption's style.

color.$description: The fill a header row, a first column and a status line take while they are kept in view, under their own fill, so that the cells passing beneath them are covered: the color of the surface the table sits on. A table on another surface (a card, a dialog, a sheet) sets that surface's color here.
The fill of every second body row of a striped table: the quietest container step above the surface, enough to carry the eye along a wide row and no more.

height.$description: Read by no behaviour of this revision: the active indicator is as tall as the row less track.padding above and below, so it has no height of its own. It stays so that the platforms still drawing the previous revision keep building; remove it in the commit that brings the last of them up to date.

gap.$description: Space between a tab's icon and its label.

height-with-icon.$description: Minimum height of a primary tab with its icon above its label. Only a medium row stacks: at small the icon stands before the label in every variant, and this is not read.

shape.$description: The corners of a tab's state layer, each at most half its height. Hover, focus and press are drawn in the box the active indicator has on that tab (selected, or as it would be if it were), never on the tab's rectangle; the focus indicator surrounds it. With the default's full corner the state layer is the indicator's capsule or circle: a layer that changes active-indicator.shape changes this with it.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

indicator-duration.$description: How long the active indicator and the underline take to slide and resize to the newly selected tab, and to settle on a tab, or return to the selected one, when a drag is released; the covered label and icon follow the indicator over the same time.

state-duration.$description: How long a tab's colors take to change between states, and how long the active indicator takes to reach the pointer when a drag is taken away from it.

transition.$description: How a row whose transition the product did not set draws a new selection (TAB-43). slide: the active indicator and the underline slide and resize to the newly selected tab over indicator-duration, the covered colors traveling with them, the two tabs' colors change over state-duration, and a tab scrolled out of view is brought in over indicator-duration. none: the new selection is drawn whole in the frame it is made — nothing travels and nothing fades. Under both a drag across the row and a Tab view's swipe still carry the indicator, because the finger moves it, and hover, focus and press are answered the same. Reduced motion draws none whatever this says. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

shape.$description: The radius of the active indicator's four corners, at most half its height: full makes it a capsule, and a circle where it is as wide as it is tall.

thickness.$description: Read by no behaviour of this revision: the line it measured is now the underline (underline.thickness). It stays so that the platforms still lagging behind the revision keep building and keep drawing their line; remove it in the commit that brings the last of them up to date.

color.$description: The icon of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it on its way across.
The label of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it, as the indicator slides across it to another tab.
A tab's label on the track.
The active indicator of primary tabs: the filled color, the strongest mark on the track.
The selected tab's label where the active indicator covers it: all of it once the indicator has landed.
The selected tab's label outside the active indicator, on the track: seen while the indicator is on its way or follows a finger, and wherever a layer's indicator does not cover the label.

emphasis.$description: How much weight the selected tab's label gains, added to the weight of label.typescale: none, because the filled active indicator already tells the selection by more than a difference of color. Every tab keeps the width its label would need at the heavier weight, so a layer that sets a weight here moves nothing when the selection does.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press mix into the selected tab.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a tab: its label's color.
The track behind the whole row in this variant: one color, the same whichever tab is selected and in every state of every tab. The tonal container's color, as a tonal Button's.

shape.$description: The radius of the underline's corners that face away from the divider. Primary's heavier line is rounded on top; secondary's stays square.

thickness.$description: The underline's thickness in this variant. Primary's is heavier than secondary's, so that two rows of underlined tabs on one screen read as main views and sub-views even where their colors are the same.

shape.$description: The radius of the active indicator's four corners, at most half its height: full makes it a capsule, and a circle where it is as wide as it is tall.

thickness.$description: Read by no behaviour of this revision: the line it measured is now the underline (underline.thickness). It stays so that the platforms still lagging behind the revision keep building and keep drawing their line; remove it in the commit that brings the last of them up to date.

color.$description: The icon of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it on its way across.
The label of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it, as the indicator slides across it to another tab.
A tab's label on the track.
The active indicator of secondary tabs: one step quieter than primary's, so that a row of sub-views under a row of main views reads as the lesser of the two on the same track.
The selected tab's label where the active indicator covers it: all of it once the indicator has landed.
The selected tab's label outside the active indicator, on the track: seen while the indicator is on its way or follows a finger, and wherever a layer's indicator does not cover the label.

emphasis.$description: How much weight the selected tab's label gains, added to the weight of label.typescale: none, because the filled active indicator already tells the selection by more than a difference of color. Every tab keeps the width its label would need at the heavier weight, so a layer that sets a weight here moves nothing when the selection does.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press mix into the selected tab.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a tab: its label's color.
The track behind the whole row in this variant: one color, the same whichever tab is selected and in every state of every tab. The tonal container's color, as a tonal Button's.

shape.$description: The radius of the underline's corners that face away from the divider.

thickness.$description: The underline's thickness in this variant.

shape.$description: The radius of the active indicator's four corners, at most half its height: full makes it a capsule, and a circle where it is as wide as it is tall.

thickness.$description: Read by no behaviour of this revision; it is here because the platforms still drawing the earlier revision read it for every variant. Remove it with primary's and secondary's.

color.$description: The icon of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it on its way across.
The label of a tab that is not selected where the active indicator covers it, as the indicator slides across it to another tab or is dragged over it.

A tab's label: the color of secondary text, which is held on the track and on every surface a row without a track may stand on. It is quieter than the selected tab's label, so that the selection is told by the label as well as by the indicator's layer.

The active indicator of tonal tabs: the quiet selection. The role named here is the tonal container's; the default system does not draw that tone — it values this token as a layer of the selected tab's own content color (selected.state-layer.color at 16%, twice the hover layer: tokens/systems/tanrei.system.json), so that the indicator is seen by the same step on the track and on whatever surface a row without a track stands on. A design system that sets this token draws what it sets.
The selected tab's label where the active indicator covers it — all of it once the indicator has landed: the content color of the tonal container, darker than the labels around it.

The selected tab's label outside the active indicator: seen while the indicator is on its way or follows a finger. It stays the quiet color there, so that the darker label is always the one under the indicator.

emphasis.$description: How much weight the selected tab's label gains, added to the weight of label.typescale, in both of its copies (where the active indicator covers it and where it does not). The tonal row's indicator is a faint layer, so its selection is also told by weight, not by color alone; every tab keeps the width its label needs at the heavier weight, so nothing moves when the selection does.

color.$description: The color hover, focus and press mix into the selected tab: the color of its content, which is drawn on the indicator. The default system also makes the indicator itself from this color.
The color hover, focus and press mix into a tab: its label's color.

The track behind the whole row in this variant: the tonal container's color, as primary's and secondary's, so that the three variants are told apart by the active indicator alone. Drawn while the row's track is on.

shape.$description: The radius of the underline's corners that face away from the divider.

thickness.$description: The underline's thickness in this variant: secondary's.

padding.$description: The space between the track's edge and what sits on it: above and below every tab's state layer and the active indicator, and between the track's ends and the first and last tab. The indicator is as tall as the row less this above and below.

shape.$description: The radius of the track's corners, at most half its height: full makes it a capsule. Tabs that scroll are clipped to it.

visible.$description: Whether a row whose track the product did not set draws its track (TAB-49). on: the track of the row's variant behind the whole row. off: no fill behind the row, which then stands on the surface it is placed on; the inset, the corners that clip a row that scrolls and every measure stay, so a row is the same size either way. A row whose track is set keeps what it was given. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

gap.$description: Distance between the glyph or the dot and the label.

shape.$description: The container's corners, capped at half its height: a pill in the default system, at any height the tag grows to. A product that wants its tags told from its chips by shape sets a step of the corner scale here.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot, at both sizes: half the glyph's box, large enough for its color to be seen beside 12 text and small enough to read as a mark, not as a glyph.

color.$description: The fill of the tag that marks the chosen one among its neighbours (the default among values, the required among fields): primary, the fill the text field's required label has.
The fill of a filled error tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
On a full fill the glyph and the dot take the label's color: a second color would not hold against the fill.
The fill of a filled info tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
The fill of a filled success tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
The fill of a filled warning tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.

size.$description: The box of the leading glyph, at both sizes: the smallest step of the icon scale, which fits the small height with the block padding (16 + 2 × 2 = 20). A tag's glyph is a mark beside a word, not a control's icon.

color.$description: The edge of an outlined tag, in every status: the one hairline, the color the divider and an outlined chip draw theirs in. Decorative: the label carries the meaning. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

width.$description: The width of an outlined tag's edge, drawn inside the container's size.

color.$description: An outlined tag has no fill: the surface behind shows through, inside the one hairline (outline.color).
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined error tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
The label of an outlined error tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined tag with no status: secondary content, quieter than the label.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined info tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
The label of an outlined info tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined success tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
The label of an outlined success tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined warning tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
The label of an outlined warning tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The quiet fill of a tag that names a category or a neutral state: the tonal role, the fill the text field's optional label has.
The fill of a tonal error tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's error form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal error tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal tag with no status: the label's color, because with no status there is nothing for a second color to say.
The fill of a tonal info tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's info form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal info tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The fill of a tonal success tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's success form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal success tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The fill of a tonal warning tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's warning form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal warning tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.

tab-size.$description: How many columns of the code face a tab character in the value advances to the next multiple of. The same count as the code block's (comp.code-block.code.tab-size): the two are one decision of a product, held equal by hand, as a component token does not alias another component's.

typescale.$description: The face of a code input's value, placeholder, prefix and suffix: the family, weight and letter spacing of the code role. Its size and line height are not taken: they are the box's (comp.input-box.input.typescale), so that a code input is as tall as any text input, sets its first line where one does, and keeps the text size below which a touch browser zooms into a box.

gap.$description: Distance between two items of the entries place on one line, and between the last item and the typing part.

row-gap.$description: Distance between two lines of the entries place when its items wrap.

typing-min-width.$description: The least width the typing part keeps beside the last item of a line; with less left, it takes a line of its own.

resize-duration.$description: How long an auto-resized multi-line input takes to change height when its number of lines changes.

inset.$description: Distance from the container's bottom edge and from its end edge to the grip's glyph.

size.$description: The glyph of the resize grip of a manually resized multi-line input: the icon scale's smallest step. Its hit area is the minimum target, not this size.

padding-inline.$description: The room on each side of a date or time segment's text, inside the highlight a focused segment is drawn with.

gap.$description: The space between two blocks of one event's body: half the regular space between two events, so what belongs to one event is closer together than two events are.

color.$description: The line that joins a marker to the next: the system's one hairline, the ring's color, the same between done and upcoming events. Decorative.

gap.$description: The space the connector keeps from the box of the marker above it and from the box of the marker below it, so the line and the markers are read as separate marks.

thickness.$description: The connector's thickness. Zero draws no connector.

color.$description: The fill of the marker of the event that is under way: the primary fill, which everywhere in the system says "the one now". The only filled marker, and the only chromatic thing a timeline draws.
The color of the mark or the glyph on that fill.
The color of the dot: secondary content, a mark beside the text and never louder than it.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot that marks an event with no status and no glyph, and of the mark inside the filled marker of the event under way: a third of the marker's box at medium, a point on the line rather than a bullet.

gap.$description: The space between the marker column and an event's content. Every event's content begins at the same edge.

color.$description: The color of a glyph inside a ring, the check of a done event included: the dot's color.

size.$description: The box of a glyph inside a ring, at both sizes: the smallest step of the icon scale, which leaves the ring clear around it.

color.$description: The ring around a glyph, around a done event's check and of an upcoming event: the system's one hairline. Decorative — the status is in the shape and in words — so it is not held to a contrast.

width.$description: The ring's width, drawn inside the marker's box.

shape.$description: A ring's corners: a circle in the default system. Never larger than half the marker's box. The dot is a circle whatever this says.

color.$description: The color of an event's time: secondary content. The only text color a timeline brings.

gap.$description: The space between an event's time and what follows it (the title, or the body where there is no title).
The space between an event's title and its body.

floating.$description: White in light schemes, lighter than the page in dark ones, as a raised surface is.
The FAB's level: a floating toolbar sits over the content as a FAB does. Level 1 is only a hairline ring in the default system, so a raised surface needs level 2 or more.
Equal to the space across the row around a medium item (64 − 40 = 2 × 12), so the items sit evenly inside the rounded ends.

docked.$description: A docked toolbar is flush with the screen's edges.

height.$description: From the container's edge to the arrow's tip. The container stands this much farther from the anchor while an arrow is drawn, so the tip keeps the offset.

inset.$description: The least distance between the arrow's base and either end of the edge it stands on. Where the form's corner radius is larger, the radius is the least distance, so the arrow never stands on a curve.

visible.$description: Whether a tooltip whose arrow the product did not set draws one (TIP-25). off: the container alone. on: a triangle on the edge that faces the anchor. A tooltip whose arrow is set keeps what it was given. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

width.$description: The arrow's base, along the container's edge.

enter-duration.$description: How long the tooltip takes to fade in, grow and travel to its place.

enter-offset.$description: How far towards the anchor from its place the tooltip starts as it fades in, and returns as it fades out. 0 fades without travelling.

enter-scale.$description: The size the tooltip grows from as it fades in, and shrinks to as it fades out, as a fraction of its own; the growth is fixed at the point of its edge that faces the anchor. 1 fades without growing.

exit-duration.$description: How long the tooltip takes to fade out, shrink and travel back.

hide-delay.$description: How long the tooltip waits after the pointer has left both the anchor and the tooltip, so the pointer can cross the offset onto the tooltip (WCAG 1.4.13, hoverable).

show-delay.$description: How long a fine pointer rests on the anchor before the tooltip opens, so that a pointer passing over it does not flash one.

warm-duration.$description: How long after a tooltip closed, because the pointer or the focus left its anchor, the next tooltip still opens at once: without its show delay and without the enter motion (TIP-28). A waiting time, kept where motion is reduced.

offset.$description: The gap between the anchor's edge and the nearest part of the tooltip, on the side the tooltip is placed: the container's edge, or the arrow's tip while an arrow is drawn. A tooltip whose offset prop is set uses that in its place.

gap.$description: Between the text and the shortcut after it.

inverse.$description: Whether a plain tooltip whose inverse the product did not set is drawn inverse (TIP-26). on: in the opposite scheme's colors, from the unprefixed tokens. off: on a surface of the scheme, from the tokens under plain.surface. A tooltip whose inverse is set keeps what it was given. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

max-width.$description: Longer text wraps onto more lines at this width.

min-height.$description: A minimum: the container grows with wrapped or enlarged text.

color.$description: The shortcut's legends and separators on the inverse container. The scheme has one content role for the inverse surface, so the shortcut takes the text's color and stands apart by the gap alone.
The container of a plain tooltip on a surface: the raised surface the rich tooltip stands on.

elevation.$description: On a surface the container's edge is its elevation, as the rich tooltip's is.

color.$description: The shortcut's legends and separators on a surface: quieter than the text.

gap.$description: Between the title and the supporting text.

inverse.$description: Whether a rich tooltip whose inverse the product did not set is drawn inverse (TIP-26). off: on a surface of the scheme, from the unprefixed tokens. on: in the opposite scheme's colors, from the tokens under rich.inverse. A tooltip whose inverse is set keeps what it was given. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

max-width.$description: Longer text wraps onto more lines at this width.

elevation.$description: As the inverse plain tooltip: apart by color, without a shadow.

color.$description: The scheme has one content role for the inverse surface; the title stands above the text by its typescale.

touch.$description: How long a tooltip opened by a long-press stays after the finger lifts. There is no hover on touch, so without it the tooltip would vanish as the finger that hid it moves away.

window-margin.$description: The least distance between the tooltip and the edges of the window's safe area; the tooltip flips, shifts or, in a window smaller than itself, covers its anchor to keep it.

shape.$description: The corners of a row's container, which its selected fill, its state layer and its focus indicator follow: a navigation drawer row's and a menu item's.

color.$description: The guide line of a tree whose guides is true: the one hairline. Decorative: the hierarchy is told by the indent and, to assistive technology, by the structure.

disclosure-duration.$description: How long a parent takes to open or close: its rows revealed or hidden, what follows moving, and its chevron turning. The name and the value of a navigation drawer group's and an accordion's.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple (as Button's).

state-duration.$description: How long a state change of a row takes.

color.$description: The quiet selection: the fill of a selected list item and of a selected destination in a navigation drawer.
What hover, focus and press mix into a selected row: its label's color.
On the selected fill every part takes the fill's own content color, which is held to contrast on it; the secondary text color is held only on surfaces.

typescale.$description: The note after the label, in both densities: the size of the compact label, at a regular weight.
The short value at the end of a row, in both densities: a navigation drawer row's trailing text.

color.$description: The chevron: a mark, quieter than the label, in the color a navigation drawer and an accordion draw theirs in.
The label: the text color of the surface the tree stands on, as a list item's headline.
What hover, focus and press mix into the row: the label's color.

brand.$description: Display and headline text. Inter for Latin, Noto Sans JP for Japanese, Noto Sans for other scripts; a product adds the Noto family of each further script it ships (Noto Sans KR, SC, TC, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai…).

icon.$description: The icon font. Material Symbols Rounded: a variable font whose weight and fill are set from sys.icon.

mono.$description: Code. Roboto Mono, with Noto Sans JP for Japanese inside code.

plain.$description: Running text and labels. Inter for Latin, Noto Sans JP for Japanese, Noto Sans for other scripts.

focus-style.$description: How keyboard focus is shown. ring: the two-tone focus ring at sys.focus offset and width. glow: the same colors as a soft halo (blurred by the ring width) instead of a hard line. Both must meet the focus contrast invariants.

link-underline.$description: When a text link is underlined. always: at rest and in every state. hover: not at rest; while the link is pointed at, focused from the keyboard or pressed. never: in no state. Read by the Link (and so by every link of long-form text) and by the breadcrumbs, each through its own component token so that a design system can set one apart; an instance can set its own. A link that is not underlined at rest is told from the text beside it by color alone, so hover and never are held by the build to a link color 3:1 apart from the text color (WCAG 1.4.1); where the platform forces its own colors the underline is drawn whatever is chosen.

pressed-feedback.$description: How a press is answered. overlay: the pressed tokens apply to the whole container at once. ripple: the pressed state layer grows from the point of contact. dim: the pressed opacity applies to the whole control and no state layer is drawn. none: no visual answer to a press (focus and hover still apply).

requirement-mark.$description: How a required control, or a required set of controls, is marked beside its label. tag: a small filled Tag holding the product's word for it. asterisk: "*" after the label's text. none: no mark is drawn; the requirement is still exposed to assistive technology. Read by the Field (and so by every composed field) and by the field group, each through its own component token so that a design system can set one apart; an instance can set its own. A label that floats inside its control's box has no room for a tag and shows tag as the asterisk. What is optional is said in words under every choice.

separation.$description: How parts that sit side by side inside one component are told apart. divider: the parts touch and a line is drawn where they meet (where the parts already differ in color, as a progress indicator's do, the edge between the colors is that line). gap: the parts are drawn apart, with empty space between them and no line. Read by the connected button group, the button with menu, the progress indicator and the menu, each through its own component token so that a design system can set one apart; an instance can set its own.

expanded.$description: The window width from which the class is expanded: there is room for navigation, and for a second column, beside the content.

medium.$description: The window width from which the class is medium. Below it the window is compact: one column, navigation over the content.

background.$description: Material 3 still publishes `background` next to `surface`; products migrating from Material 2 bind to it.

elevation-ring.$description: The hairline ring that edges an elevated surface. Separate from `outline-variant` so a product can outline elevated surfaces more or less strongly than it draws dividers.

error.$description: Something failed or is destructive. Every product with a form or a delete button needs it.

error-container.$description: Something failed or is destructive. Every product with a form or a delete button needs it.

focus-ring.$description: The keyboard focus indicator (its outer stroke). Separate from `primary` because a product may want a saturated brand color and a calmer, or more visible, focus ring.

focus-ring-inner.$description: The optional inner stroke of the focus indicator: a second tone that keeps the indicator visible where the outer one would blend into the background.

info.$description: Neutral, non-urgent system information, distinct from the brand color so notices do not read as calls to action.

info-container.$description: Neutral, non-urgent system information, distinct from the brand color so notices do not read as calls to action.

inverse-link.$description: Inline text links on `inverse-surface`. Separate from `inverse-primary` for the reason `link` is separate from `primary`: a product whose links are not its brand color needs them told as links on a surface of the opposite theme too, and a layer that re-points `link` and `inverse-link` has recolored every text link and nothing else.

inverse-surface.$description: A surface of the opposite theme inside the current one (snackbars, tooltips).

link.$description: Inline text links. Separate from `primary` because links sit in running text and must read as links, whatever the brand color is.

on-error.$description: Something failed or is destructive. Every product with a form or a delete button needs it.

on-error-container.$description: Something failed or is destructive. Every product with a form or a delete button needs it.

on-info.$description: Neutral, non-urgent system information, distinct from the brand color so notices do not read as calls to action.

on-info-container.$description: Neutral, non-urgent system information, distinct from the brand color so notices do not read as calls to action.

on-primary.$description: The product's main action and brand emphasis. Separate from every other intent because a product's brand color is rarely its error, success or link color.

on-primary-container.$description: The product's main action and brand emphasis. Separate from every other intent because a product's brand color is rarely its error, success or link color.

on-primary-fixed.$description: Material 3's `on-primary-fixed`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-primary-fixed-variant.$description: Material 3's `on-primary-fixed-variant`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-secondary.$description: Lower-emphasis actions and selections (tonal buttons, chips) that must not compete with the primary action.

on-secondary-container.$description: Lower-emphasis actions and selections (tonal buttons, chips) that must not compete with the primary action.

on-secondary-fixed.$description: Material 3's `on-secondary-fixed`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-secondary-fixed-variant.$description: Material 3's `on-secondary-fixed-variant`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-success.$description: Something succeeded or is valid: form validation, completed steps, positive status.

on-success-container.$description: Something succeeded or is valid: form validation, completed steps, positive status.

on-surface.$description: Primary text and icons on any surface.

on-surface-variant.$description: Secondary text and icons: supporting copy, placeholders, inactive icons.

on-tertiary.$description: Material Design 3 has a third accent family for contrast and balance. It is particular to that system, so this preset declares it instead of Tanrei carrying the slot for everyone. Tones the reference publishes are fixed to its exact colors; any other tone is generated.

on-tertiary-container.$description: Material Design 3 has a third accent family for contrast and balance. on-tertiary-fixed.$description: Material 3's `on-tertiary-fixed`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-tertiary-fixed-variant.$description: Material 3's `on-tertiary-fixed-variant`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

on-warning.$description: Something needs attention before it becomes an error: caution banners, risky choices.

on-warning-container.$description: Something needs attention before it becomes an error: caution banners, risky choices.

outline.$description: A boundary people must be able to see to identify a control (an input's border, an unchecked checkbox): at least 3:1.

outline-variant.$description: A decorative hairline (dividers, card edges). Separate from `outline` because a product wants quiet dividers without losing visible input borders.

primary.$description: The product's main action and brand emphasis. Separate from every other intent because a product's brand color is rarely its error, success or link color.

primary-container.$description: The product's main action and brand emphasis. Separate from every other intent because a product's brand color is rarely its error, success or link color.

primary-fixed.$description: Material 3's `primary-fixed`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

primary-fixed-dim.$description: Material 3's `primary-fixed-dim`: a color that stays the same in light and dark, for content that must keep its hue across themes.

surface.$description: The default background of a view.

surface-bright.$description: A background that stays bright in dark schemes (bars that must separate from a dark canvas).

surface-container.$description: Container step 3 of 5: the default container.

surface-container-highest.$description: Container step 5 of 5: inputs and chips that sit on other containers.

surface-container-lowest.$description: The lowest of five container steps. One product nests cards in panels in pages, so it needs several distinguishable steps at once.

surface-dim.$description: A background that recedes behind `surface` (wells, the area around a sheet).

surface-tint.$description: Material 3's tint for tonal elevation overlays.

surface-variant.$description: A differently weighted surface for low-emphasis fills such as tracks.

tertiary.$description: Material Design 3 has a third accent family for contrast and balance. It is particular to that system, so this preset declares it instead of Tanrei carrying the slot for everyone. Tones the reference publishes are fixed to its exact colors; any other tone is generated.

level0.$description: No elevation: an empty list of shadow layers, so nothing is drawn.

inner-width.$description: Width of the optional inner stroke. 0 = a single-tone ring.

offset.$description: Distance from the control's edge to the indicator. Negative draws the indicator inside the control.

selected.$description: The same icon, selected, is filled (FILL 1).

unselected.$description: An icon for something that is not selected is outlined (FILL 0).

weight.$description: The stroke weight of a control's own mark (the `wght` axis of the icon font). A mark is a glyph of the same icon set as every icon, drawn at the small steps of the icon scale on a fill of the control; the default system draws it heavier than sys.icon.weight so that its stroke is wider than a pixel there.

max.$description: The largest optical size the icon font draws (Material Symbols: 48).

min.$description: The smallest optical size the icon font draws (Material Symbols: 20).

weight.$description: The stroke weight of every icon (the `wght` axis of the icon font).

press-hold.$description: The shortest time a pressed state stays visible. A tap or a keyboard activation is over in a frame; without a floor the feedback cannot be seen.

stagger.$description: Delay between items in a sequential reveal.

corner-smoothing.$description: How a corner's curve eases into the straight edge, 0–1, with Figma's meaning: 0 is a quarter circle, 0.6 is the iOS continuous corner, 1 the most eased curve. The radius does not change. Platforms differ in the curve they can draw: on Apple's platforms SwiftUI's continuous corner (RoundedCornerStyle.continuous) is one fixed curve with no amount, drawn for every amount above 0; on the web, CSS corner-shape: superellipse() takes the amount where the browser has it (Chromium-based browsers, WebKit 26.6), and the corner is a quarter circle where it does not.

full.$description: Opt-in only: avatars, badges, segmented controls, pill variants.

small.$description: Default for controls: buttons, inputs, menu items, tooltips.

body.$description: p: the default text of an interface.

body-small.$description: small: secondary text, one step down.

display.$description: The one hero size: a landing screen's statement, a splash. Not a heading level.

body.$description: How much weight `emphasized` text gains, per family: a platform adds it to the role's weight. The default system adds 100 to every family.

display.$description: How much weight `emphasized` text gains, per family: a platform adds it to the role's weight. The default system adds 100 to every family.

heading.$description: How much weight `emphasized` text gains, per family: a platform adds it to the role's weight. The default system adds 100 to every family.

label.$description: How much weight `emphasized` text gains, per family: a platform adds it to the role's weight. The default system adds 100 to every family.

eyebrow.$description: A section's kicker above a heading: small, tracked wide, uppercase by the component (the token stores no text transform).

heading-4.$description: h4: a group inside a section.

heading-5.$description: h5, and the title of a card, dialog or list item.

heading-6.$description: h6, and a table's or a form section's heading.

label.$description: Text inside and next to controls: buttons, inputs, navigation.
